as well as the Purāṇa that grants devotion to Viṣṇu and is superior to the Veda,
Rādhā, the cowherd women born of his body, and the ever-worshipful brāhmaṇas—
they are boiled in a pit, O gods, for a duration equal to Brahmā's lifetime,
head downward, legs upward, encircled by swarms of serpents,
devoured by monstrous worms resembling snakes;
exceedingly distressed and terrified, they wail unceasingly.
Distraught, they surely consume phlegm, urine, and feces;
and the enraged servants of Yama thrust firebrands into their mouths.
Threatening them at the three junctures of the day, they beat them with rods,
and out of fear they make those who are thirsty from the blows drink urine.
Then, in another cosmic cycle, at the initial creation of the Creator once more,
their remedy will come about,” so spoke the lotus-born [Brahmā].
“Surely by reviling Śiva the gods will go to hell.
Do you wish to render just this kind of help, O sons?

4.40.s:
brahmaṇā prerito dakṣo dattvā śūlabhṛte sutām ..
na pāpaṃ paramaiśvaryaṃ saṃprāpa haranindakaḥ .. 47 ..
anicchayā sutāṃ dattvā turyapuṇyaṃ lalābha saḥ ..
aho vihāya sārūpyaṃ tucchaṃ svargaṃ lalābha saḥ .. 48 ..
kaścinmadhye ca yuṣmākaṃ gatvā śailagṛhaṃ surāḥ ..
saṃpādayatu svamataṃ śailendrasya prayatnataḥ .. 49 ..
4.40.d:
ब्रह्मणा प्रेरितो दक्षो दत्त्वा शूलभृते सुताम् ॥
न पापं परमैश्वर्यं संप्राप हरनिन्दकः ॥ 47 ॥
अनिच्छया सुतां दत्त्वा तुर्यपुण्यं ललाभ सः ॥
अहो विहाय सारूप्यं तुच्छं स्वर्गं ललाभ सः ॥ 48 ॥
कश्चिन्मध्ये च युष्माकं गत्वा शैलगृहं सुराः ॥
संपादयतु स्वमतं शैलेन्द्रस्य प्रयत्नतः ॥ 49 ॥

4.40.s:
anicchayā sutāṃ dattvā sukhaṃ tiṣṭhatu bhārate ..
tasmai bhaktyā sutāṃ dattvā mokṣaṃ prāpsyati niścitam .. 4.40.150 ..
paścātsaptarṣayaḥ sarve gṛhītvā tāmarundhatīm ..
dhruvaṃ tasya gṛhaṃ gatvā bodhayiṣyanti parvatam .. 51 ..
vinā pinākinaṃ durgā varaṃ nānyaṃ variṣyati ..
anicchayā sutāṃ tasmai pradāsyati sutājñayā .. 52 ..
4.40.d:
अनिच्छया सुतां दत्त्वा सुखं तिष्ठतु भारते ॥
तस्मै भक्त्या सुतां दत्त्वा मोक्षं प्राप्स्यति निश्चितम् ॥ 4.40.150 ॥
पश्चात्सप्तर्षयः सर्वे गृहीत्वा तामरुन्धतीम् ॥
ध्रुवं तस्य गृहं गत्वा बोधयिष्यन्ति पर्वतम् ॥ 51 ॥
विना पिनाकिनं दुर्गा वरं नान्यं वरिष्यति ॥
अनिच्छया सुतां तस्मै प्रदास्यति सुताज्ञया ॥ 52 ॥

4.40.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ devā gacchantu mandiram ..
ityuktvā vākpatiḥ śīghraṃ tapase svarṇadīṃ gataḥ .. 153 ..
4.40.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं देवा गच्छन्तु मन्दिरम् ॥
इत्युक्त्वा वाक्पतिः शीघ्रं तपसे स्वर्णदीं गतः ॥ 153 ॥
4.40.m:
Thus all has been told; let the gods return to their abode.”
Having spoken thus, the Lord of Speech promptly went to the river of heaven for austerities.

4.41.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
tadā devāḥ samālocya jagmuste brahmaṇo'ntikam ..
sarve nivedanaṃ cakrurbrahmāṇaṃ jagatāṃ patim .. 1 ..
4.41.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
तदा देवाः समालोच्य जग्मुस्ते ब्रह्मणोऽन्तिकम् ॥
सर्वे निवेदनं चक्रुर्ब्रह्माणं जगतां पतिम् ॥ 1 ॥

4.41.s:
devā ūcuḥ .. ..
tava sṛṣṭau jagatsraṣṭā ratnādhāro himālayaḥ ..
sa cetprāpsyati mokṣaṃ ca ratnagarbhā kuto mahī .. 2 ..
4.41.d:
देवा ऊचुः ॥ ॥
तव सृष्टौ जगत्स्रष्टा रत्नाधारो हिमालयः ॥
स चेत्प्राप्स्यति मोक्षं च रत्नगर्भा कुतो मही ॥ 2 ॥

4.41.s:
sutāṃ śūlabhṛte dattvā bhaktyā śaileśvaraḥ svayam ..
nārāyaṇasya sārūpyaṃ saṃprāpsyati na saṃśayaḥ .. 3 ..
4.41.d:
सुतां शूलभृते दत्त्वा भक्त्या शैलेश्वरः स्वयम् ॥
नारायणस्य सारूप्यं संप्राप्स्यति न संशयः ॥ 3 ॥

4.41.s:
tvaṃ tasya nindanaṃ kṛtvā vimatiṃ pratipādaya ..
tvayā vinā kṣamo nānyo gaccha śailagṛhe prabho .. 4 ..
4.41.d:
त्वं तस्य निन्दनं कृत्वा विमतिं प्रतिपादय ॥
त्वया विना क्षमो नान्यो गच्छ शैलगृहे प्रभो ॥ 4 ॥

4.41.s:
devānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā tānuvāca vidhiḥ svayam ..
vacanaṃ nītisāraṃ ca karṇapīyūṣamuttamam .. 5 .. ..
4.41.d:
देवानां वचनं श्रुत्वा तानुवाच विधिः स्वयम् ॥
वचनं नीतिसारं च कर्णपीयूषमुत्तमम् ॥ 5 ॥ ॥

4.41.s:
.. brahmovāca ..
nāhaṃ kartuṃ kṣamo vatsāḥ śivanindāṃ suduṣkarām ..
saṃpadvināśarūpāṃ ca vipado bījarūpiṇīm .. 6 ..
4.41.d:
॥ ब्रह्मोवाच ॥
नाहं कर्तुं क्षमो वत्साः शिवनिन्दां सुदुष्कराम् ॥
संपद्विनाशरूपां च विपदो बीजरूपिणीम् ॥ 6 ॥

4.41.s:
bhūteśaṃ prasthāpayata svātmanindāṃ karoti saḥ ..
paranindā vināśāya svanindā yaśase param ..7..
4.41.d:
भूतेशं प्रस्थापयत स्वात्मनिन्दां करोति सः ॥
परनिन्दा विनाशाय स्वनिन्दा यशसे परम् ॥7॥

4.41.s:
brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā taṃ praṇamya surāḥ priye..
śīghraṃ yayuste kailāsaṃ gatvā ca tuṣṭuvuḥ śivam .. 8 ..
4.41.d:
ब्रह्मणो वचनं श्रुत्वा तं प्रणम्य सुराः प्रिये॥
शीघ्रं ययुस्ते कैलासं गत्वा च तुष्टुवुः शिवम् ॥ 8 ॥

4.41.s:
sarve nivedanaṃ cakruḥ śaṃkaraṃ karuṇālayam ..
sa yayau śailamūlaṃ ca tānāśvāsya prahasya ca .. 9 ..
4.41.d:
सर्वे निवेदनं चक्रुः शंकरं करुणालयम् ॥
स ययौ शैलमूलं च तानाश्वास्य प्रहस्य च ॥ 9 ॥

4.41.s:
devā mumudire sarve śīghraṃ gatvā svamandiram ..
iṣṭasiddhirmude śaśvadasiddhirduḥkhavardhinī .. 4.41.10 ..
4.41.d:
देवा मुमुदिरे सर्वे शीघ्रं गत्वा स्वमन्दिरम् ॥
इष्टसिद्धिर्मुदे शश्वदसिद्धिर्दुःखवर्धिनी ॥ 4.41.10 ॥

4.41.s:
atha śailaḥ sabhāmadhye samuvāsa mudā'nvitaḥ ..
bandhuvargaiḥ parivṛtaḥ pārvatīsahitaḥ svayam ..11..
4.41.d:
अथ शैलः सभामध्ये समुवास मुदाऽन्वितः ॥
बन्धुवर्गैः परिवृतः पार्वतीसहितः स्वयम् ॥11॥
4.41.m:
Then the mountain [king], filled with joy, sat in the midst of the assembly
surrounded by his kinsfolk, accompanied by Pārvatī herself.

4.41.s:
etasminnantare tatra viprarūpī śivaḥ svayam ..
samājagāma sahasā prasannavadanekṣaṇaḥ .. 12 ..
4.41.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र विप्ररूपी शिवः स्वयम् ॥
समाजगाम सहसा प्रसन्नवदनेक्षणः ॥ 12 ॥
4.41.m:
At that moment, Śiva himself, in the form of a brāhmaṇa,
suddenly arrived there with a joyful face and eyes.

4.41.s:
daṇḍī chatrī dīrghavāsā bibhrattilakamuttamam ..
kare sphaṭikamālāṃ ca śālagrāmaṃ gale dadhat .. 13 ..
4.41.d:
दण्डी छत्री दीर्घवासा बिभ्रत्तिलकमुत्तमम् ॥
करे स्फटिकमालां च शालग्रामं गले दधत् ॥ 13 ॥
4.41.m:
Carrying a staff and an umbrella, wearing long garments, bearing an excellent tilaka,
holding a crystal rosary in his hand and a Śāligrāma on his neck, [he came].

4.41.s:
taṃ ca dṛṣṭvā samuttasthau sagaṇaśca himālayaḥ ..
nanāma daṇḍavadbhūmau bhaktyā'tithimapūrvakam ..14..
4.41.d:
तं च दृष्ट्वा समुत्तस्थौ सगणश्च हिमालयः ॥
ननाम दण्डवद्भूमौ भक्त्याऽतिथिमपूर्वकम् ॥14॥
4.41.m:
And seeing him, Himālaya stood up together with his attendants,
and bowed like a staff upon the ground with devotion to that unprecedented guest.

4.41.s:
nanāma pārvatī bhaktyā prāṇeśaṃ viprarūpiṇam ..
āśiṣaṃ yuyuje vipraḥ sarveṣāṃ prītipūrvakam .. 15 ..
4.41.d:
ननाम पार्वती भक्त्या प्राणेशं विप्ररूपिणम् ॥
आशिषं युयुजे विप्रः सर्वेषां प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ॥ 15 ॥
4.41.m:
Pārvatī bowed with devotion to the lord of her life, who had assumed the form of a brahmin.
The brahmin affectionately bestowed a blessing upon everyone.

4.41.s:
śailadattāsane śīghramuvāsa brāhmaṇaḥ svayam ..
madhuparkādikaṃ sarvaṃ jagrāha prītipūrvakam .. 16 ..
4.41.d:
शैलदत्तासने शीघ्रमुवास ब्राह्मणः स्वयम् ॥
मधुपर्कादिकं सर्वं जग्राह प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ॥ 16 ॥
4.41.m:
The brāhmaṇa himself quickly sat down upon the seat offered by the Mountain,
and affectionately accepted all [the hospitality], beginning with the madhuparka.

4.41.s:
papraccha kuśalaṃ śailo brāhmaṇaṃ ko bhavāniti ..
uvāca sarvaṃ viprendro girīndraṃ sādareṇa ca .. 17 ..
4.41.d:
पप्रच्छ कुशलं शैलो ब्राह्मणं को भवानिति ॥
उवाच सर्वं विप्रेन्द्रो गिरीन्द्रं सादरेण च ॥ 17 ॥
4.41.m:
The Mountain inquired of his well-being, asking the brāhmaṇa, "Who are you?"
The foremost of brahmins respectfully said everything to the king of mountains.

4.41.s:
.. brāhmaṇa uvāca ..
ghāṭikāṃ vṛttimāśritya bhramāmi dharaṇītale ..
manoyāyī sarvagāmī sarvajño'haṃ gurorvarāt .. 18 ..
4.41.d:
॥ ब्राह्मण उवाच ॥
घाटिकां वृत्तिमाश्रित्य भ्रमामि धरणीतले ॥
मनोयायी सर्वगामी सर्वज्ञोऽहं गुरोर्वरात् ॥ 18 ॥
4.41.m:
"Relying upon the livelihood of a wandering astrologer, I wander over the surface of the earth.
By the boon of my guru, I travel at the speed of thought, I go everywhere, and I know all.

4.41.s:
mayā jñātaṃ śaṃkarāya sutāṃ dātuṃ tvamicchasi ..
imāṃ padmāsamāṃ divyāmajñātakulaśīline .. 19 ..
4.41.d:
मया ज्ञातं शंकराय सुतां दातुं त्वमिच्छसि ॥
इमां पद्मासमां दिव्यामज्ञातकुलशीलिने ॥ 19 ॥
4.41.m:
I have learned that you wish to give your daughter to Śaṅkara—
this divine girl, equal to Lakṣmī, to one whose lineage and character are unknown,

4.41.s:
nirāśrayāyāsaṅgayārūpāya nirguṇāya ca..
śmaśānagāmine sarvabhūtanāthāya yogine .. 4.41.20 ..
4.41.d:
निराश्रयायासङ्गयारूपाय निर्गुणाय च॥
श्मशानगामिने सर्वभूतनाथाय योगिने ॥ 4.41.20 ॥
4.41.m:
who is shelterless, unattached, formless, and devoid of gunas,
who frequents cremation grounds, the lord of all bhūtas, an ascetic yogin,

4.41.s:
digvāsase'higātrāya vibhūtibhūṣaṇāya ca ..
vyālagrāhisvarūpāya kālavyāpādanāya ca..21..
4.41.d:
दिग्वाससेऽहिगात्राय विभूतिभूषणाय च ॥
व्यालग्राहिस्वरूपाय कालव्यापादनाय च॥21॥
4.41.m:
clothed in the directions, whose body is wrapped in snakes, and adorned with sacred ashes,
whose appearance is that of a snake-catcher, the destroyer of death,

4.41.s:
ajñātamṛtyave'jñāyānāthāyābandhave bhave..
taptasvarṇajaṭābhāradhāriṇe nirdhanāya ca .. 22 ..
4.41.d:
अज्ञातमृत्यवेऽज्ञायानाथायाबन्धवे भवे॥
तप्तस्वर्णजटाभारधारिणे निर्धनाय च ॥ 22 ॥
4.41.m:
whose death is unknown, without master, without kinsmen in the world,
bearing a mass of matted hair like molten gold, and penniless,

4.41.s:
ajñātavayase'tīva vṛddhāya cāvikāriṇe..
sarvāśrayāya bhramiṇe nāgahārāya bhikṣave .. 23 ..
4.41.d:
अज्ञातवयसेऽतीव वृद्धाय चाविकारिणे॥
सर्वाश्रयाय भ्रमिणे नागहाराय भिक्षवे ॥ 23 ॥
4.41.m:
whose age is unknown, extremely old, yet changeless,
the refuge of all, a wanderer, wearing a necklace of serpents, a beggar.

4.41.s:
nibodha jñānināṃ śreṣṭhaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ kulodbhavam ..
sa te pātrānurūpaśca pārvatīdātṛkarmaṇi .. 24 ..
4.41.d:
निबोध ज्ञानिनां श्रेष्ठं नारायणं कुलोद्भवम् ॥
स ते पात्रानुरूपश्च पार्वतीदातृकर्मणि ॥ 24 ॥
4.41.m:
Know Nārāyaṇa, the best of the wise, born of a noble family;
he is the suitable bridegroom for you in giving Pārvatī away.

4.41.s:
mahājanaḥ smeramukhaḥ śrutimātrādbhaviṣyati ..
lakṣaśailādhipastvaṃ ca na tasyaiko'sti bāndhavaḥ .. 25 ..
4.41.d:
महाजनः स्मेरमुखः श्रुतिमात्राद्भविष्यति ॥
लक्षशैलाधिपस्त्वं च न तस्यैकोऽस्ति बान्धवः ॥ 25 ॥
4.41.m:
The great people will smile mockingly merely upon hearing [of this match].
You are the lord of a hundred thousand mountains, whereas he does not have a single relative.

4.41.s:
bāndhavānmenakāṃ praśnaṃ kuru śīghraṃ prayatnataḥ..
sarvānpṛccha ca yatnena he bandho pārvatīṃ vinā .. 26 ..
4.41.d:
बान्धवान्मेनकां प्रश्नं कुरु शीघ्रं प्रयत्नतः॥
सर्वान्पृच्छ च यत्नेन हे बन्धो पार्वतीं विना ॥ 26 ॥
4.41.m:
Inquire quickly and carefully of your relatives and of Menakā;
ask everyone with care, O friend—except Pārvatī.

4.41.s:
rogiṇe nauṣadhaṃ śaśvatkupathyaṃ rocate sadā ..
ityuktvā brāhmaṇaḥ śīghraṃ snātvā bhuktvā mudā'nvitaḥ ..27 ..
4.41.d:
रोगिणे नौषधं शश्वत्कुपथ्यं रोचते सदा ॥
इत्युक्त्वा ब्राह्मणः शीघ्रं स्नात्वा भुक्त्वा मुदाऽन्वितः ॥27 ॥
4.41.m:
Medicine never pleases a sick person, but unwholesome food always does."
Having spoken thus, the brāhmaṇa quickly bathed, ate with joy,

4.41.s:
jagāma svālayaṃ śānto vṛndāvanavinodini ..
brāhmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā menovāca himālayam ..
śokena sāśrunayanā hṛdayena vidūyatā .. 28 ..
4.41.d:
जगाम स्वालयं शान्तो वृन्दावनविनोदिनि ॥
ब्राह्मणस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मेनोवाच हिमालयम् ॥
शोकेन साश्रुनयना हृदयेन विदूयता ॥ 28 ॥
4.41.m:
and, being tranquil, departed to his own abode, O you who delight in Vṛndāvana.
Having heard the brāhmaṇa's words, Menā spoke to Himālaya,
her eyes filled with tears of grief, her heart burning with sorrow.

4.41.s:
menakovāca ..
śṛṇu śailendra madvākyaṃ pariṇāmasukhāvaham .. 29 ..
4.41.d:
मेनकोवाच ॥
शृणु शैलेन्द्र मद्वाक्यं परिणामसुखावहम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.41.m: "Listen, O king of mountains, to my words which will bring happiness in the end.

4.41.s:
pṛccha śailavarānasmai na dāsyāmi sutāmaham ..
tyakṣyāmi sarvānviṣayānbhakṣyāmi viṣameva ca .. 4.41.30 ..
4.41.d:
पृच्छ शैलवरानस्मै न दास्यामि सुतामहम् ॥
त्यक्ष्यामि सर्वान्विषयान्भक्ष्यामि विषमेव च ॥ 4.41.30 ॥
4.41.m:
Ask the foremost mountains! I will not give my daughter to him.
I will abandon all worldly possessions, and I will even consume poison;

4.41.s:
gale baddhvā'mbikāṃ paśya yāsyāmi ghorakānanam ..
gṛhītvā pārvatīṃ menā gatvā kopālayaṃ ruṣā ..31..
4.41.d:
गले बद्ध्वाऽम्बिकां पश्य यास्यामि घोरकाननम् ॥
गृहीत्वा पार्वतीं मेना गत्वा कोपालयं रुषा ॥31॥
4.41.m:
taking Ambikā by the neck, behold, I will go to a dreadful forest!"
Taking Pārvatī, Menā went in anger to the chamber of wrath.

4.41.s:
tyaktvā''hāraṃ rudantī ca cakāra śayanaṃ bhuvi..
etasminnantare tatra vasiṣṭho bhrātṛbhiḥ saha .. 32 ..
4.41.d:
त्यक्त्वा'ऽहारं रुदन्ती च चकार शयनं भुवि॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र वसिष्ठो भ्रातृभिः सह ॥ 32 ॥
4.41.m:
Refusing food and weeping, she lay down upon the ground.
In the meantime, Vasiṣṭha arrived there together with his brothers,

4.41.s:
ājagāma punastaiśca yuktā paścādarundhatī ..
praṇamya śailastānsarvānsvarṇasiṃhāsanaṃ dadau .. 33 ..
4.41.d:
आजगाम पुनस्तैश्च युक्ता पश्चादरुन्धती ॥
प्रणम्य शैलस्तान्सर्वान्स्वर्णसिंहासनं ददौ ॥ 33 ॥
4.41.m:
and Arundhatī also came along behind them.
Bowing to all of them, the Mountain offered them golden thrones.

4.41.s:
dattvā ṣoḍaśopacārānpūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ ..
ṛṣayaśca sabhāmadhye sukhamūṣuḥ sukhāsane .. 34 ..
4.41.d:
दत्त्वा षोडशोपचारान्पूजयामास भक्तितः ॥
ऋषयश्च सभामध्ये सुखमूषुः सुखासने ॥ 34 ॥
4.41.m:
Presenting the sixteen articles of worship, he honoured them with devotion.
And the ṛṣis sat comfortably upon comfortable seats in the midst of the assembly.

4.41.s:
jagāmārundhatī tūrṇaṃ yatra menā ca pārvatī..
gatvā dadarśa menāṃ ca śayānāṃ śokamūrcchitām .. 35 ..
4.41.d:
जगामारुन्धती तूर्णं यत्र मेना च पार्वती॥
गत्वा ददर्श मेनां च शयानां शोकमूर्च्छिताम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.41.m:
Arundhatī quickly went to where Menā and Pārvatī were.
Having gone, she saw Menā lying down, fainting from sorrow.

4.41.s:
uvāca madhuraṃ sādhvī sāvadhānāṃ hitaṃ vacaḥ ..
arundhatyuvāca ..
uttiṣṭha menake sādhvi tvadgṛhe'hamarundhatī .. 36 ..
4.41.d:
उवाच मधुरं साध्वी सावधानां हितं वचः ॥
अरुन्धत्युवाच ॥
उत्तिष्ठ मेनके साध्वि त्वद्गृहेऽहमरुन्धती ॥ 36 ॥
4.41.m:
The virtuous woman gently spoke beneficial words to the attentive [Menā].
"Arise, virtuous Menakā! I, Arundhatī, am in your home.

4.41.s:
pitṝṇāṃ mānasī kanyā māṃ jānīhi vidhervadhūm ..
arundhatyāḥ svaraṃ śrutvā śīghramutthāya menakā ..
uvāca śirasā natvā tāṃ padmāmiva tejasā .. 37 ..
4.41.d:
पितॄणां मानसी कन्या मां जानीहि विधेर्वधूम् ॥
अरुन्धत्याः स्वरं श्रुत्वा शीघ्रमुत्थाय मेनका ॥
उवाच शिरसा नत्वा तां पद्मामिव तेजसा ॥ 37 ॥
4.41.m:
Know me as the mind-born daughter of the ancestors, the daughter-in-law of Brahmā."
Hearing Arundhatī's voice, Menakā quickly arose,
and bowing her head, spoke to her who resembled Lakṣmī in splendour.

4.41.s:
menakovāca ..
aho'dya kimidaṃ puṇyamasmākaṃ puṇyajanmanām .. 38 ..
4.41.d:
मेनकोवाच ॥
अहोऽद्य किमिदं पुण्यमस्माकं पुण्यजन्मनाम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.41.m: "Ah, what merit is this today for us who are born of merit!

4.41.s:
vadhūrjagadvidheḥ patnī vasiṣṭhasya mamālaye ..
saṃbhrameṇedamevokte gṛhaṃ te'haṃ ca kiṃkarī .. .. 39 ..
4.41.d:
वधूर्जगद्विधेः पत्नी वसिष्ठस्य ममालये ॥
संभ्रमेणेदमेवोक्ते गृहं तेऽहं च किंकरी ॥ ॥ 39 ॥
4.41.m:
The daughter-in-law of the Creator of the universe, the wife of Vasiṣṭha, is in my home!
Having spoken this with agitation, [she said:] 'This house is yours, and I am your servant.

4.41.s:
īśvarī jagatāṃ sraṣṭurāgatā bahupuṇyataḥ ..
pādyaṃ dattvā svarṇapīṭhe vāsayāmāsa tāṃ satīm .. 4.41.40 ..
4.41.d:
ईश्वरी जगतां स्रष्टुरागता बहुपुण्यतः ॥
पाद्यं दत्त्वा स्वर्णपीठे वासयामास तां सतीम् ॥ 4.41.40 ॥
4.41.m:
The mistress [belonging to the family] of the creator of the worlds has come because of great merit!'"
Having offered water for washing the feet, she seated that chaste woman upon a golden stool.

4.41.s:
bhojayāmāsa miṣṭānnaṃ bubhuje kanyayā saha ..
śivasya hetornītiṃ ca bodhayāmāsa menakām .. 41 ..
4.41.d:
भोजयामास मिष्टान्नं बुभुजे कन्यया सह ॥
शिवस्य हेतोर्नीतिं च बोधयामास मेनकाम् ॥ 41 ॥
4.41.m:
She fed her sweet food, and dined together with the maiden;
and, for Śiva’s sake, she instructed Menakā in proper conduct. // 41

4.41.s:
arundhatī prasaṅgena saṃbandhayojanāni ca ..
atha śailamṛṣīndrāśca nītisāraṃ paraṃ vacaḥ ..
bodhayāmāsuḥ saṃbandhayojanāni prasaṅgataḥ .. 42 ..
4.41.d:
अरुन्धती प्रसङ्गेन संबन्धयोजनानि च ॥
अथ शैलमृषीन्द्राश्च नीतिसारं परं वचः ॥
बोधयामासुः संबन्धयोजनानि प्रसङ्गतः ॥ 42 ॥
4.41.m:
In the course of conversation, Arundhatī also explained the suitability of the union.
Then the foremost of sages addressed the mountain with words embodying the essence of right counsel,
and in the course of conversation they explained the suitability of the union. // 42

4.41.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
śailendra śrūyatāṃ vākyamasmākaṃ śubhakārakam .. 43 ..
4.41.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
शैलेन्द्र श्रूयतां वाक्यमस्माकं शुभकारकम् ॥ 43 ॥
4.41.m: O king of mountains, listen to our speech, which brings good fortune! // 43

4.41.s:
śivāya pārvatīṃ dehi saṃhartuḥ śvaśuro bhava ..
ayācitāraṃ deveśaṃ bodhayāśu prayatnataḥ .. 44 ..
4.41.d:
शिवाय पार्वतीं देहि संहर्तुः श्वशुरो भव ॥
अयाचितारं देवेशं बोधयाशु प्रयत्नतः ॥ 44 ॥
4.41.m:
Give Pārvatī to Śiva; become the father-in-law of the Destroyer!
Carefully and swiftly make your intention known to the Lord of the gods, who asks for nothing. // 44

4.41.s:
tava śaṅkāvināśāya brahmasaṃbandhakarmaṇi ..
necchako dārasaṃyoge śaṃkaro yogināṃ varaḥ .. 45 ..
4.41.d:
तव शङ्काविनाशाय ब्रह्मसंबन्धकर्मणि ॥
नेच्छको दारसंयोगे शंकरो योगिनां वरः ॥ 45 ॥
4.41.m:
For the dispelling of your doubt regarding the act of alliance with Brahman:
Śaṅkara, the best of yogins, has no desire for union with a wife. // 45

4.41.s:
vidheḥ prārthanayā deva tava kanyāṃ grahīṣyati..
duhituste tapasyānte pratijñānaṃ cakāra saḥ .. 46 ..
4.41.d:
विधेः प्रार्थनया देव तव कन्यां ग्रहीष्यति॥
दुहितुस्ते तपस्यान्ते प्रतिज्ञानं चकार सः ॥ 46 ॥
4.41.m:
At Brahmā’s request, O king, he will accept your daughter;
and at the end of your daughter’s ascetic austerities, he made a promise to her. // 46

4.41.s:
hetudvayena yogīndro vivāhaṃ ca kariṣyati ..
ṛṣīṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā prahasya ca himālayaḥ ..
uvāca kiṃcidbhītaśca paraṃ vinayapūrvakam .. 47 ..
4.41.d:
हेतुद्वयेन योगीन्द्रो विवाहं च करिष्यति ॥
ऋषीणां वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य च हिमालयः ॥
उवाच किंचिद्भीतश्च परं विनयपूर्वकम् ॥ 47 ॥
4.41.m:
For these two reasons, the lord of yogins will marry her.
Hearing the words of the sages, Himālaya smiled,
and somewhat afraid, he spoke with the utmost humility: // 47

4.41.s:
himālaya uvāca ..
śivasya rājasāmagrīṃ na hi paśyāmi kāṃcana ..
kiṃcidāśramamaiśvaryaṃ kiṃ vā svajanabāndhavam .. 48 ..
4.41.d:
हिमालय उवाच ॥
शिवस्य राजसामग्रीं न हि पश्यामि कांचन ॥
किंचिदाश्रममैश्वर्यं किं वा स्वजनबान्धवम् ॥ 48 ॥
4.41.m:
I do not see any royal possessions of Śiva at all,
nor any dwelling, sovereign power, or kinsmen and relatives. // 48

4.41.s:
na kanyāmatinirliptayogine dātumarhati ..
yūyaṃ vidhātuḥ putrāśca satyaṃ vadata niścitam .. 49 ..
4.41.d:
न कन्यामतिनिर्लिप्तयोगिने दातुमर्हति ॥
यूयं विधातुः पुत्राश्च सत्यं वदत निश्चितम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.41.m:
It is not fitting to give a maiden to an utterly detached yogin.
You are the sons of the Creator; speak the plain truth! // 49

4.41.s:
nānurūpāya putrāya pitā kanyā dadāti cet ..
kālāllobhādbhayānmohācchatābdaṃ narakaṃ vrajet .. 4.41.50 ..
4.41.d:
नानुरूपाय पुत्राय पिता कन्या ददाति चेत् ॥
कालाल्लोभाद्भयान्मोहाच्छताब्दं नरकं व्रजेत् ॥ 4.41.50 ॥
4.41.m:
If a father gives his maiden daughter to an unsuitable youth,
out of the pressure of circumstances, greed, fear, or delusion, he goes to hell for a hundred years. // 50

4.41.s:
na hi dāsyāmyahaṃ kanyāmicchayā śūlapāṇine ..
yadvidhānaṃ bhavedyogyamṛṣayastadvidhīyatām .. 51 ..
4.41.d:
न हि दास्याम्यहं कन्यामिच्छया शूलपाणिने ॥
यद्विधानं भवेद्योग्यमृषयस्तद्विधीयताम् ॥ 51 ॥
4.41.m:
I certainly will not voluntarily give my daughter to the spear-bearer.
Whatever course may be proper, O sages, let that be done! // 51

4.41.s:
himālayavacaḥ śrutvā vasiṣṭho vidhinandanaḥ ..
vedavedāṅgavijñātā vedoktaṃ vaktumudyataḥ .. 52 ..
4.41.d:
हिमालयवचः श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठो विधिनन्दनः ॥
वेदवेदाङ्गविज्ञाता वेदोक्तं वक्तुमुद्यतः ॥ 52 ॥
4.41.m:
Hearing Himālaya’s speech, Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahmā,
knowing the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, prepared to speak what is declared in the Veda. // 52

4.41.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca ..
vacanaṃ vividhaṃ śaila laukike vaidike tathā ..
sarvaṃ jānāti śāstrajño nirmalajñānacakṣuṣā .. 53 ..
4.41.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ॥
वचनं विविधं शैल लौकिके वैदिके तथा ॥
सर्वं जानाति शास्त्रज्ञो निर्मलज्ञानचक्षुषा ॥ 53 ॥
4.41.m:
O mountain, speech is of diverse kinds in worldly and Vedic matters;
one who knows the scriptures understands everything by the eye of stainless knowledge. // 53

4.41.s:
asatyamahitaṃ paścātsāmprataṃ śrutisundaram ..
subuddhaṃ śatrurvadati na hitaṃ ca kadācana .. 54 ..
4.41.d:
असत्यमहितं पश्चात्साम्प्रतं श्रुतिसुन्दरम् ॥
सुबुद्धं शत्रुर्वदति न हितं च कदाचन ॥ 54 ॥
4.41.m:
An enemy speaks what is false and harmful later, but currently pleasing to the ear,
and with clever understanding, he never speaks what is truly beneficial. // 54

4.41.s:
āpātaprītijanakaṃ pariṇāmasukhāvaham ..
dayālurdharmaśīlaśca bodhayatyeva bāndhavam .. .. 55 ..
4.41.d:
आपातप्रीतिजनकं परिणामसुखावहम् ॥
दयालुर्धर्मशीलश्च बोधयत्येव बान्धवम् ॥ ॥ 55 ॥
4.41.m:
One who is compassionate and virtuous instructs a kinsman
with words that are immediately pleasing and bring happiness in the end. // 55

4.41.s:
śrutimātrātsudhātulyaṃ sarvakāle sukhāvaham ..
satyasāraṃ hitakaraṃ vacasāṃ śreṣṭhamīpsitam .. 56 ..
4.41.d:
श्रुतिमात्रात्सुधातुल्यं सर्वकाले सुखावहम् ॥
सत्यसारं हितकरं वचसां श्रेष्ठमीप्सितम् ॥ 56 ॥
4.41.m:
What is like nectar merely upon hearing, brings happiness at all times,
is the essence of truth, is beneficial, and is the best and most desired of speeches. // 56

4.41.s:
evaṃ ca trividhaṃ śaila nītiśāstranirūpitam ..
kathyatāṃ triṣu madhye kiṃ vadāmi vākyamīpsitam ..57..
4.41.d:
एवं च त्रिविधं शैल नीतिशास्त्रनिरूपितम् ॥
कथ्यतां त्रिषु मध्ये किं वदामि वाक्यमीप्सितम् ॥57॥
4.41.m:
Thus, O mountain, three kinds of speech are laid down in the treatises on conduct.
Tell me, among these three, which desired speech shall I speak? // 57

4.41.s:
bāhyasaṃpadvihīnaśca śaṃkarastridaśeśvaraḥ ..
tattvajñānasamudreṣu sannimagnaikamānasaḥ ..58 ..
4.41.d:
बाह्यसंपद्विहीनश्च शंकरस्त्रिदशेश्वरः ॥
तत्त्वज्ञानसमुद्रेषु सन्निमग्नैकमानसः ॥58 ॥
4.41.m:
Śaṅkara, the lord of the gods, is devoid of external wealth,
with his single mind deeply immersed in the oceans of knowledge of reality. // 58

4.41.s:
āpātabhramasaṃpattirvidyucchrīriva nāśinī ..
sadānandasyeśvarasya svātmārāmasya kā spṛhā .. 59 ..
4.41.d:
आपातभ्रमसंपत्तिर्विद्युच्छ्रीरिव नाशिनी ॥
सदानन्दस्येश्वरस्य स्वात्मारामस्य का स्पृहा ॥ 59 ॥
4.41.m:
Perceived wealth is an illusion, perishable like the flash of lightning.
What desire could there be for the Lord who is eternal bliss, delighting in his own self? // 59

4.41.s:
gṛhī dadāti svasutāṃ rājyasaṃpattiśāline ..
kanyāṃ vidveṣiṇe dattvā kanyāghātī bhavetpitā .. 4.41.60 ..
4.41.d:
गृही ददाति स्वसुतां राज्यसंपत्तिशालिने ॥
कन्यां विद्वेषिणे दत्त्वा कन्याघाती भवेत्पिता ॥ 4.41.60 ॥
4.41.m:
A householder gives his daughter to one who possesses the wealth of a kingdom;
by giving a maiden to a hostile person, a father becomes a slayer of his daughter. // 60

4.41.s:
ko vadecchaṃkaro duḥkhī kubero yasya kiṃkaraḥ..
bhrūbhaṅgalīlayā sṛṣṭiṃ sraṣṭuṃ naṣṭuṃ kṣamo hi yaḥ..61..
4.41.d:
को वदेच्छंकरो दुःखी कुबेरो यस्य किंकरः॥
भ्रूभङ्गलीलया सृष्टिं स्रष्टुं नष्टुं क्षमो हि यः॥61॥
4.41.m:
Who could say that Śaṅkara is destitute, when Kubera is his servant,
and when he is able to create and destroy the universe by a mere play of his brow? // 61

4.41.s:
nirguṇaḥ paramātmā ca ya īśaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ ..
sarveśaḥ sa ca nirlipto liptaśca sarvajantuṣu .. 62 ..
4.41.d:
निर्गुणः परमात्मा च य ईशः प्रकृतेः परः ॥
सर्वेशः स च निर्लिप्तो लिप्तश्च सर्वजन्तुषु ॥ 62 ॥
4.41.m:
He is the Lord without gunas, the Paramātman, beyond Prakṛti;
he is the Lord of all, detached, yet abiding within all living beings. // 62

4.41.s:
sa ekaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhāre sa sarvaḥ sṛṣṭikarmaṇi ..
nirākāraśca sākāro vibhuḥ svecchāmayaḥ svayam .. 63 ..
4.41.d:
स एकः सृष्टिसंहारे स सर्वः सृष्टिकर्मणि ॥
निराकारश्च साकारो विभुः स्वेच्छामयः स्वयम् ॥ 63 ॥
4.41.m:
He is one in the dissolution of creation, and he is all in the act of creation;
he is formless, with form, the all-pervading Lord whose nature is his own will. // 63

4.41.s:
ya īśastrividhāṃ mūrtiṃ vidhatte sṛṣṭikarmaṇi ..
sṛṣṭisthityantajananīṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivābhidhām..64..
4.41.d:
य ईशस्त्रिविधां मूर्तिं विधत्ते सृष्टिकर्मणि ॥
सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तजननीं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवाभिधाम्॥64॥
4.41.m:
That Lord assumes a threefold form in the work of creation,
bringing about creation, maintenance, and destruction, named Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. // 64

4.41.s:
brahmā ca brahmalokastho viṣṇuḥ kṣīrodavāsakṛt ..
śivaḥ kailāsavāsī ca sarvāḥ kṛṣṇavibhūtayaḥ .. 65 ..
4.41.d:
ब्रह्मा च ब्रह्मलोकस्थो विष्णुः क्षीरोदवासकृत् ॥
शिवः कैलासवासी च सर्वाः कृष्णविभूतयः ॥ 65 ॥
4.41.m:
Brahmā dwells in Brahmaloka, Viṣṇu resides in the ocean of milk,
and Śiva dwells on Kailāsa; all are manifestations of Kṛṣṇa. // 65

4.41.s:
śrīkṛṣṇaśca dvidhābhūto dvibhujaśca caturbhujaḥ ..
caturbhujaśca vaikuṇṭhe goloke dvibhujaḥ svayam ..66 ..
4.41.d:
श्रीकृष्णश्च द्विधाभूतो द्विभुजश्च चतुर्भुजः ॥
चतुर्भुजश्च वैकुण्ठे गोलोके द्विभुजः स्वयम् ॥66 ॥

4.41.s:
tasya devasya teṃ'śāśca brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ ..
keciddevāḥ kalāstasya kalāṃśāścaiva kecana .. 67 ..
4.41.d:
तस्य देवस्य तेंऽशाश्च ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ॥
केचिद्देवाः कलास्तस्य कलांशाश्चैव केचन ॥ 67 ॥
4.41.m:
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are portions of that Lord;
certain gods are his parts, and some are fractions of parts. // 67

4.41.s:
kṛṣṇaḥ sṛṣṭyunmukhaścāpi prakṛtiṃ tatra nirmame ..
nirmāya tāṃ ca tadyonau vīryādhānaṃ cakāra ha ..68..
4.41.d:
कृष्णः सृष्ट्युन्मुखश्चापि प्रकृतिं तत्र निर्ममे ॥
निर्माय तां च तद्योनौ वीर्याधानं चकार ह ॥68॥
4.41.m:
Intent on creating, Kṛṣṇa fashioned Prakṛti there;
having fashioned her, he deposited his seed in her womb. // 68

4.41.s:
tato ḍimbhaḥ samudbhūtastanmadhye ca mahāvirāṭ ..
mahāviṣṇuḥ sa vijñeyo śrīkṛṣṇaṣoḍaśāṃśakaḥ .. 69 ..
4.41.d:
ततो डिम्भः समुद्भूतस्तन्मध्ये च महाविराट् ॥
महाविष्णुः स विज्ञेयो श्रीकृष्णषोडशांशकः ॥ 69 ॥
4.41.m:
From that arose an egg, and within it the great Virāj.
He is to be known as Mahāviṣṇu, a sixteenth portion of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

4.41.s:
nābhipadmodbhavo brahmā tasyaiva jalaśāyinaḥ ..
bhālodbhavastasya sraṣṭuḥ śaṃkaraścandraśekharaḥ .. 4.41.70 ..
4.41.d:
नाभिपद्मोद्भवो ब्रह्मा तस्यैव जलशायिनः ॥
भालोद्भवस्तस्य स्रष्टुः शंकरश्चन्द्रशेखरः ॥ 4.41.70 ॥
4.41.m:
Brahmā arose from the navel-lotus of that very one who lies upon the waters;
from the forehead of that creator arose Śaṅkara, the moon-crested.

4.41.s:
mahāviṣṇurvāmapārśvātsaṃbhūto viṣṇureva ca ..
sarve prākṛtikāḥ śaila brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ .. 71 ..
4.41.d:
महाविष्णुर्वामपार्श्वात्संभूतो विष्णुरेव च ॥
सर्वे प्राकृतिकाः शैल ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादयः ॥ 71 ॥
4.41.m:
And from the left side of Mahāviṣṇu, Viṣṇu himself was born.
All of them—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others—are born of Prakṛti, O Mountain.

4.41.s:
dhatte caturvidhāṃ mūrtiṃ prakṛtiḥ kṛṣṇasaṃbhavā ..
aṃśena līlayā sṛṣṭyai kalayā bahudhā tayā ..72..
4.41.d:
धत्ते चतुर्विधां मूर्तिं प्रकृतिः कृष्णसंभवा ॥
अंशेन लीलया सृष्ट्यै कलया बहुधा तया ॥72॥
4.41.m:
Prakṛti, born of Kṛṣṇa, assumes a fourfold form,
by a portion, in sport, for creation, [and] in manifold ways by that part.

4.41.s:
kṛṣṇavāmāṃgasaṃbhūtā rādhā rāseśvarī svayam ..
mukhodbhavā svayaṃ vāṇī rāgādhiṣṭhātṛdevatā .. 73 ..
4.41.d:
कृष्णवामांगसंभूता राधा रासेश्वरी स्वयम् ॥
मुखोद्भवा स्वयं वाणी रागाधिष्ठातृदेवता ॥ 73 ॥
4.41.m:
Born from Kṛṣṇa's left side is Rādhā herself, the queen of the rāsa-dance.
Born from his mouth is Sarasvatī herself, the presiding deity of musical melodies.

4.41.s:
vakṣaḥsthalodbhavā lakṣmīḥ sarvasaṃpatsvarūpiṇī ..
śivā tejaḥsu devānāmāvirbhāvaṃ cakāra sā .. 74 ..
4.41.d:
वक्षःस्थलोद्भवा लक्ष्मीः सर्वसंपत्स्वरूपिणी ॥
शिवा तेजःसु देवानामाविर्भावं चकार सा ॥ 74 ॥
4.41.m:
Born from his chest is Lakṣmī, the embodiment of all prosperity.
Śivā manifested herself from the splendours of the gods;

4.41.s:
nihatya dānavānsarvāndevebhyaśca śriyaṃ dadau ..
prāpya kalpāṃtare janma jaṭhare dakṣayoṣitaḥ .. 79 ..
4.41.d:
निहत्य दानवान्सर्वान्देवेभ्यश्च श्रियं ददौ ॥
प्राप्य कल्पांतरे जन्म जठरे दक्षयोषितः ॥ 79 ॥
4.41.m:
having slain all the Dānavas, she bestowed royal fortune upon the gods.
Having obtained birth in another kalpa in the womb of Dakṣa's wife,

4.41.s:
nāmnā satī śivaṃ prāpa dakṣastasmai dadau ca tām ..
yogena dehaṃ tatyāja śrutvā sā bhartṛniṃdanam..76..
4.41.d:
नाम्ना सती शिवं प्राप दक्षस्तस्मै ददौ च ताम् ॥
योगेन देहं तत्याज श्रुत्वा सा भर्तृनिंदनम्॥76॥
4.41.m:
known by the name Satī, she attained Śiva, and Dakṣa gave her to him.
Through yoga she abandoned her body upon hearing her husband reviled.

4.41.s:
pitṝṇāṃ mānasī kanyā menakā tava gehinī ..
lalābha tasyā jaṭhare janma sā jagadaṃbikā .. 77 ..
4.41.d:
पितॄणां मानसी कन्या मेनका तव गेहिनी ॥
ललाभ तस्या जठरे जन्म सा जगदंबिका ॥ 77 ॥
4.41.m:
Menakā, the mind-born daughter of the ancestors, is your wife;
in her womb that mother of the universe took birth.

4.41.s:
śivā śivasya patnīyaṃ śaila janmanijanmani ..
kalpe kalpe buddhirūpā jñānināṃ jananī parā ..78...
4.41.d:
शिवा शिवस्य पत्नीयं शैल जन्मनिजन्मनि ॥
कल्पे कल्पे बुद्धिरूपा ज्ञानिनां जननी परा ॥78॥।
4.41.m:
This Śivā is the wife of Śiva, O Mountain, birth after birth,
in kalpa after kalpa, having the form of intellect, the supreme mother of the wise,

4.41.s:
jatismarā ca sarvajñā siddhidā siddhirūpiṇī ..
asyā asthicitābhasma bhaktyā dhatte śivaḥ svayama..79..
4.41.d:
जतिस्मरा च सर्वज्ञा सिद्धिदा सिद्धिरूपिणी ॥
अस्या अस्थिचिताभस्म भक्त्या धत्ते शिवः स्वयम॥79॥
4.41.m:
remembering her past births, omniscient, bestowing perfection, embodying perfection.
Śiva himself reverently wears the ashes of her funeral pyre and bones.

4.41.s:
dehi tvaṃ svecchayā kanyāṃ dehi bhadra śivāya ca ..
athavā sā svayaṃ kāṃtasthānaṃ yāsyati drakṣyati ..4.41.80..
4.41.d:
देहि त्वं स्वेच्छया कन्यां देहि भद्र शिवाय च ॥
अथवा सा स्वयं कांतस्थानं यास्यति द्रक्ष्यति ॥4.41.80॥
4.41.m:
Give your daughter of your own free will; give her to Śiva, O blessed one!
Otherwise, she will go on her own to her beloved's abode; you will see.

4.41.s:
prāktanādyasya yā kāṃtā sā taṃ prāpnoti vallabham ..
prajāpaternibaṃdhaṃ ca na ko'pi khaṃḍituṃ kṣamaḥ ..81..
4.41.d:
प्राक्तनाद्यस्य या कांता सा तं प्राप्नोति वल्लभम् ॥
प्रजापतेर्निबंधं च न कोऽपि खंडितुं क्षमः ॥81॥
4.41.m:
Whoever is one's beloved from past deeds attains that husband;
and no one is able to break the decree of the creator.

4.41.s:
vivāhe notsukaḥ śaṃbhuḥ svātmārāmaśca tattvavit ..
tuṣṭuvustaṃ surāḥ sarve tārakākhyena pīḍitāḥ .. 82 ..
4.41.d:
विवाहे नोत्सुकः शंभुः स्वात्मारामश्च तत्त्ववित् ॥
तुष्टुवुस्तं सुराः सर्वे तारकाख्येन पीडिताः ॥ 82 ॥
4.41.m:
Śambhu, rejoicing in his own Self and knowing the truth, was not eager for marriage;
all the gods, afflicted by the one named Tāraka, praised him.

4.41.s:
devānāṃ pīḍanaṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmaṇā prārthito vibhuḥ ..
kṛpayā svīcakārāśu kṛpālurdevasaṃsadi .. 83 ..
4.41.d:
देवानां पीडनं दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मणा प्रार्थितो विभुः ॥
कृपया स्वीचकाराशु कृपालुर्देवसंसदि ॥ 83 ॥
4.41.m:
Seeing the affliction of the gods, being entreated by Brahmā, the all-pervading Lord,
the compassionate one, out of grace swiftly accepted in the assembly of the gods.

4.41.s:
kṛtvā pratijñāṃ yogīṃdro dṛṣṭvā kleśamasaṃkhyakam ..
duhituste tapaḥsthānamājagāma dvijātmakaḥ .. 84 ..
4.41.d:
कृत्वा प्रतिज्ञां योगींद्रो दृष्ट्वा क्लेशमसंख्यकम् ॥
दुहितुस्ते तपःस्थानमाजगाम द्विजात्मकः ॥ 84 ॥
4.41.m:
Having made a vow, the king of yogins, seeing innumerable afflictions,
came in the form of a brāhmaṇa to the place of your daughter's austerities.

4.41.s:
tāmāśvāsya varaṃ dattvā jagāma nijamaṃdiram ..
tacchrutvaivāyayuḥ sarve surāḥ śakrādayo mudā .. 85 ..
4.41.d:
तामाश्वास्य वरं दत्त्वा जगाम निजमंदिरम् ॥
तच्छ्रुत्वैवाययुः सर्वे सुराः शक्रादयो मुदा ॥ 85 ॥
4.41.m:
Consoling her and granting her a boon, he departed to his own abode.
Hearing that, all the gods headed by Śakra came in joy,

4.41.s:
nārāyaṇaśca bhagavānbrahmā dharmaśca sāṃpratam ..
ṛṣayo munayaḥ sarve gaṃdharvā yakṣarākṣasāḥ .. 86 ..
4.41.d:
नारायणश्च भगवान्ब्रह्मा धर्मश्च सांप्रतम् ॥
ऋषयो मुनयः सर्वे गंधर्वा यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ 86 ॥
4.41.m:
and Lord Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, and Dharma now,
all the ṛṣis, munis, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas.

4.41.s:
tatra sarve mudā yuktaiḥ samālocanakartṛbhiḥ ..
prasthāpitā vayaṃ śīghramanṛṇā sā aruṃdhatī.. 87 ..
4.41.d:
तत्र सर्वे मुदा युक्तैः समालोचनकर्तृभिः ॥
प्रस्थापिता वयं शीघ्रमनृणा सा अरुंधती॥ 87 ॥
4.41.m:
There, having conferred together with joy,
we were dispatched quickly, [along with] the faultless Arundhatī.

4.41.s:
tava prabodhane prītirvarddhate mahatī sadā ..
saṃprāptaṃ śubhakāryaṃ ca sarvakālasukhāvaham .. 88 ..
4.41.d:
तव प्रबोधने प्रीतिर्वर्द्धते महती सदा ॥
संप्राप्तं शुभकार्यं च सर्वकालसुखावहम् ॥ 88 ॥
4.41.m:
Great joy ever increases in instructing you;
an auspicious undertaking has arrived, bringing happiness for all time.

4.41.s:
śivāṃ śivāya śaileṃdra svecchayā cenna dāsyasi .. .
bhavitā vā vivāhaśca bhavitavyabalena ca .. 89 ..
4.41.d:
शिवां शिवाय शैलेंद्र स्वेच्छया चेन्न दास्यसि ॥ ।
भविता वा विवाहश्च भवितव्यबलेन च ॥ 89 ॥
4.41.m: If you do not give Śivā to Śiva of your own will, O king of mountains, / the marriage will still take place by the power of destiny.

4.41.s:
āgamiṣyati devo yo nārāyaṇasahāyavān ..
ratnasārarathe kṛtvā devānāṃ pravaraṃ varam .. 4.41.90 ..
4.41.d:
आगमिष्यति देवो यो नारायणसहायवान् ॥
रत्नसाररथे कृत्वा देवानां प्रवरं वरम् ॥ 4.41.90 ॥
4.41.m:
The god who has Nārāyaṇa as his ally will come,
having placed in a chariot of the essence of gems the foremost bridegroom among the gods,

4.41.s:
yogīṃdrāṇāṃ vareṇyaṃ taṃ jñānināṃ ca gurorgurum ..
ādimadhyāṃtarahitamavikāramajaṃ param .. 91 ..
4.41.d:
योगींद्राणां वरेण्यं तं ज्ञानिनां च गुरोर्गुरुम् ॥
आदिमध्यांतरहितमविकारमजं परम् ॥ 91 ॥
4.41.m:
the choice one among kings of yogins, the guru of gurus to the wise,
free from beginning, middle, and end, changeless, unborn, supreme.

4.41.s:
varaṃ dadau śivāyai sa śivaśca tapasaḥ sthale ..
na hīśvarapratijñātaṃ durlabhaṃ viphalaṃ bhavet .. 92 ..
4.41.d:
वरं ददौ शिवायै स शिवश्च तपसः स्थले ॥
न हीश्वरप्रतिज्ञातं दुर्लभं विफलं भवेत् ॥ 92 ॥
4.41.m:
That Śiva granted a boon to Śivā at the site of her austerity;
surely what is promised by the Lord, rare to attain, cannot become fruitless.

4.41.s:
brahmādistaṃbaparyataṃ sarvaṃ naśvaramasthiram ..
aho pratijñā durlaṅghyā sādhūnāmavināśinī .. 93 ..
4.41.d:
ब्रह्मादिस्तंबपर्यतं सर्वं नश्वरमस्थिरम् ॥
अहो प्रतिज्ञा दुर्लङ्घ्या साधूनामविनाशिनी ॥ 93 ॥
4.41.m:
From Brahmā down to a blade of grass, everything is perishable and unstable.
Ah, the vow of the virtuous is inviolable and imperishable!

4.41.s:
eko maheṃdraḥ śailānāṃ pakṣāṃściccheda līlayā ..
pavano līlayā meroḥ śṛṃgabhaṃgaṃ cakāra ha .. .. 94 ..
4.41.d:
एको महेंद्रः शैलानां पक्षांश्चिच्छेद लीलया ॥
पवनो लीलया मेरोः शृंगभंगं चकार ह ॥ ॥ 94 ॥
4.41.m:
Mahendra alone cut off the wings of the mountains in sport;
the Wind in sport shattered the peak of Meru.

4.41.s:
ke vā śaileṣu yoddhāraḥ suraiḥ saha himālaya ..
patiṣyaṃti samudreṣu pavanaiḥ preritāḥ kṣaṇāt .. 95 ..
4.41.d:
के वा शैलेषु योद्धारः सुरैः सह हिमालय ॥
पतिष्यंति समुद्रेषु पवनैः प्रेरिताः क्षणात् ॥ 95 ॥
4.41.m:
Who among the mountains are fighters against the gods, O Himālaya?
Impelled by winds, they will fall into the oceans in an instant.

4.41.s:
ekārthe yadi śailendra sarvasaṃpadvinaśyati ..
sarvānrakṣati taddattvā vinā ca śaraṇāgatam .. 96 ..
4.41.d:
एकार्थे यदि शैलेन्द्र सर्वसंपद्विनश्यति ॥
सर्वान्रक्षति तद्दत्त्वा विना च शरणागतम् ॥ 96 ॥
4.41.m:
If for the sake of one thing, O king of mountains, all wealth is ruined,
giving that up, one preserves everything, except one who has sought refuge.

4.41.s:
śaraṇāgatarakṣārthaṃ prāṇāṃśca dātumarhati ..
putradāradhanaṃ sarvāniti nītivido viduḥ .. 97 ..
4.41.d:
शरणागतरक्षार्थं प्राणांश्च दातुमर्हति ॥
पुत्रदारधनं सर्वानिति नीतिविदो विदुः ॥ 97 ॥
4.41.m:
For the protection of one who has sought refuge, one ought to give even life,
sons, wife, wealth, all—so know those who understand statecraft.

4.41.s:
dattvā viprāya svasutāmanaraṇyo nṛpeśvara ..
brahmaśāpādvimuktaśca rarakṣa sarvasaṃpadam .. 98 ..
4.41.d:
दत्त्वा विप्राय स्वसुतामनरण्यो नृपेश्वर ॥
ब्रह्मशापाद्विमुक्तश्च ररक्ष सर्वसंपदम् ॥ 98 ॥
4.41.m:
King Anaraṇya, having given his daughter to a brāhmaṇa, O king,
became freed from a brāhmaṇa's curse and preserved all his prosperity.

4.41.s:
tamāśu bodhayāmāsurnītiśāstravido janāḥ ..
brahmaśāpanimagnaṃ ca brahmaṇyamatikātaram .. 99 ..
4.41.d:
तमाशु बोधयामासुर्नीतिशास्त्रविदो जनाः ॥
ब्रह्मशापनिमग्नं च ब्रह्मण्यमतिकातरम् ॥ 99 ॥
4.41.m:
Men who understood treatises on statecraft quickly instructed him.
plunged in a brāhmaṇa’s curse, devoted to brāhmaṇas, and exceedingly distressed:

4.41.s:
tvameva śailarājeṃdra sutāṃ dattvā śivāya ca ..
rakṣa sarvānbaṃdhuvargānvaśe kuru surānapi .. 4.41.100 ..
4.41.d:
त्वमेव शैलराजेंद्र सुतां दत्त्वा शिवाय च ॥
रक्ष सर्वान्बंधुवर्गान्वशे कुरु सुरानपि ॥ 4.41.100 ॥
4.41.m:
“O lord of kings of mountains, you alone, by giving your daughter to Śiva,
protect all your kinsmen and bring even the gods under control!”

4.41.s:
vasiṣṭhasya vacaḥ śrutvā prahasya parvateśvaraḥ ..
papraccha nṛpavṛttāṃtaṃ hṛdayena vidūyatā .. 101 ..
4.41.d:
वसिष्ठस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य पर्वतेश्वरः ॥
पप्रच्छ नृपवृत्तांतं हृदयेन विदूयता ॥ 101 ॥
4.41.m:
Having heard the words of Vasiṣṭha, the lord of mountains smiled,
and with an aching heart he asked about the king’s history:

4.41.s:
himālaya uvāca ..
kasya vaṃśodbhavo brahmannanaraṇyo nṛpeśvaraḥ ..
sutāṃ dattvā sa ca kathamarakṣatsarvasaṃpadam .. 102 ..
4.41.d:
हिमालय उवाच ॥
कस्य वंशोद्भवो ब्रह्मन्ननरण्यो नृपेश्वरः ॥
सुतां दत्त्वा स च कथमरक्षत्सर्वसंपदम् ॥ 102 ॥
4.41.m:
“In whose lineage was Anaraṇya, the lord of kings, born, O brāhmaṇa?
And how did he, by giving his daughter, protect all his fortune?”

4.41.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca ..
manuvaṃśodbhavo rājā so'naraṇyo nṛpeśvaraḥ ..
ciṃrajīvī dharmaśīlo vaiṣṇavo vijiteṃdriyaḥ .. 103 ..
4.41.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ॥
मनुवंशोद्भवो राजा सोऽनरण्यो नृपेश्वरः ॥

अपुत्रको नृपश्रेष्ठस्तपसे पुष्करं गतः ॥
सुचिरं च तपस्तप्त्वा वरं लब्ध्वा महेश्वरात् ॥ ॥ 4.41.120 ॥
संप्राप्य वैष्णवं पुत्रमनरण्यं जितेंद्रियम् ॥
दत्त्वा तस्मै च राज्यं च जगाम तपसे वनम् ॥ 21 ॥
अनरण्यो नृपश्रेष्ठः सप्तद्वीपमहीपतिः ॥
चकार यज्ञशतकं भृगुणा च पुरोधसा॥22॥
तुच्छं मत्वाशु शक्रत्वं न लेभे नश्वरं सुधीः ॥
लीलया च जितः शक्रो लीलया च जितो बलिः ॥23॥
जिताश्च दानवेंद्रा वै ज्वलता स्वेन तेजसा ॥
बभूवुः शतपुत्राश्च राज्ञस्तस्य हिमालय ॥24॥
कन्यैका सुंदरी रम्या पद्मा पद्मालयासमा॥
सा कन्या यौवनस्था च बभूव पितृमंदिरे॥25॥
चारं प्रस्थापयमास वराय नृपतीश्वरः ॥
एकदा पिप्पलादश्च गंतुं स्वाश्रममुत्सुकः॥26॥
तपःस्थाने निर्जने च गन्धर्वं स ददर्श ह ॥
स्त्रीषु निर्मग्नचित्तं च शृङ्गाररससागरे ॥27॥
4.41.m:
Childless, that best of kings went to Puṣkara for austerities;
having performed austerities for a very long time and received a boon from Maheśvara,
having obtained a Vaiṣṇava son, Anaraṇya, whose senses were conquered,
and having given the kingdom to him, he went to the forest for austerities.
Anaraṇya, best of kings, ruler of the earth with its seven continents,
performed a hundred sacrifices with Bhṛgu as his family priest.
Considering the status of Śakra insignificant and perishable, the wise [king] did not take it;
effortlessly Śakra was conquered, and effortlessly Bali was conquered,
and the lords of the Dānavas were conquered by his blazing brilliance.
A hundred sons were born to that king, O Himālaya,
and one beautiful, delightful daughter, Padmā, equal to the dweller on the lotus.
That maiden reached youth in her father’s house.
The lord of kings dispatched an emissary to seek a bridegroom.
Once, Pippalāda, eager to go to his own hermitage,
saw a Gandharva in a solitary place of austerity,
with mind immersed in women, in the ocean of erotic sentiment,

ददर्श पद्मां युवती पद्मामिव मनोरमाम् ॥
केयं कस्येति पप्रच्छ समीपस्थाञ्जनान्मुनिः ॥ 4.41.130 ॥

राजा शीघ्रं मुनिं दृष्ट्वा प्रणनाम भयाकुलः ॥ 32 ॥
मधुपर्कादिकं दत्त्वा पूजयामास भक्तितः ॥
कामात्सर्वं गृहीत्वा च ययाचे कन्यकां मुनिः ॥ 33 ॥

4.41.m:
saw a young maiden named Padmā, charming like Lakṣmī.
The sage asked the people standing nearby, "Who is this, and whose [daughter]?"
The people informed him: "Padmā, the daughter of Anaraṇya."
The sage, having bathed and worshipped his chosen deity, the lord of Rādhikā,
went, filled with desire, to the courtyard of Anaraṇya's royal assembly for alms.
Quickly seeing the sage, the king bowed down, agitated by fear.
Accepting everything, the sage, through desire, asked for the maiden.
The king became silent, unable to utter anything.
The sage asked him again: "O king, give me your maiden!
Otherwise, in an instant I will turn everything to ashes."
All the attendants were overwhelmed by the sage's splendor.
The king wept along with his attendants, seeing him old and afflicted by decrepitude.
All the queens wept, helpless as to what should be done.

The chief queen, the mother of the girl, fainted, overwhelmed with grief.
A wise scholar, versed in the science of polity, instructed the king,
the queen, and the royal princes in the supreme propriety regarding a maiden:

To whom else could you give her, to an outsider other than a brahmin?
I see no worthy recipient in the three worlds other than a brahmin.

राजकन्यानिमित्तेन सर्वसंपत्प्रणश्यति ॥ 4.41.140 ॥
सर्वं रक्षति तत्त्यक्त्वा विना तं शरणागतम् ॥

4.41.m:
Give your daughter to the sage and protect all your prosperity!
On account of a princess, all wealth is destroyed;
[a wise man] protects everything by abandoning that, except for one who has sought refuge."
Hearing the wise man's words and lamenting again and again,
the king adorned his daughter and truly gave her to the lord of sages.
Taking his beloved, the sage, delighted, went to his own abode.
The king, renouncing everything, departed to perform austerities in sorrow.
From grief over her husband and her daughter, the beautiful woman gave up her life.
Without the king, his sons, grandsons, and servants fell into a swoon.

karmaṇā manasā vācā lakṣmīrnārāyaṇaṃ yathā .. 1 ..
4.42.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ॥
अथानरण्यस्य कन्या सिषेवे भक्तितो मुनिम् ॥
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा लक्ष्मीर्नारायणं यथा ॥ 1 ॥
4.42.m: Then, Anaraṇya's daughter served the sage with devotion,

4.42.s:
ekadā svarṇadīṃ snātuṃ gacchaṃtīṃ sasmitāṃ satīm ..
dadarśa pathi dharmaśca māyayā nṛpaliṃgakaḥ .. 2 ..
4.42.d:
एकदा स्वर्णदीं स्नातुं गच्छंतीं सस्मितां सतीम् ॥
ददर्श पथि धर्मश्च मायया नृपलिंगकः ॥ 2 ॥

4.42.s:
cāruratnarathasthaśca ratnālaṃkārabhūṣitaḥ ..
navīnayauvanaśrīmānkāmadevasamaprabhaḥ ..3..
4.42.d:
चारुरत्नरथस्थश्च रत्नालंकारभूषितः ॥
नवीनयौवनश्रीमान्कामदेवसमप्रभः ॥3॥

4.42.s:
dṛṣṭvā tāṃ sundarīṃ ramyāmuvāca māyayā vibhuḥ ..
vijñātumantastattvaṃ ca tasyāśca muniyoṣitaḥ .. 4 ..
4.42.d:
दृष्ट्वा तां सुन्दरीं रम्यामुवाच मायया विभुः ॥
विज्ञातुमन्तस्तत्त्वं च तस्याश्च मुनियोषितः ॥ 4 ॥

4.42.s:
dharma uvāca ..
ayi sundari lakṣmīva rājayogye manohare ..
atīva yauvanasthe ca kāmini sthirayauvane..5..
4.42.d:
धर्म उवाच ॥
अयि सुन्दरि लक्ष्मीव राजयोग्ये मनोहरे ॥
अतीव यौवनस्थे च कामिनि स्थिरयौवने॥5॥

4.42.s:
jarāturasya vṛddhasya samīpe tvaṃ na rājase ..
candanāgurusaṃliptā rājase rājavakṣasi..6..
4.42.d:
जरातुरस्य वृद्धस्य समीपे त्वं न राजसे ॥
चन्दनागुरुसंलिप्ता राजसे राजवक्षसि॥6॥

4.42.s:
vipraṃ tapaḥsu nirataṃ satyajñaṃ maraṇonmukham..
vihāya paśya rājendraṃ ratiśūraṃ smarāturam ..7..
4.42.d:
विप्रं तपःसु निरतं सत्यज्ञं मरणोन्मुखम्॥
विहाय पश्य राजेन्द्रं रतिशूरं स्मरातुरम् ॥7॥

4.42.s:
prāpnoti sundaraṃ puṇyātsaundaryaṃ pūrvajanmataḥ ..
saphalaṃ tadbhavetsarvaṃ rasikāliṃganena ca .. 8 ..
4.42.d:
प्राप्नोति सुन्दरं पुण्यात्सौन्दर्यं पूर्वजन्मतः ॥
सफलं तद्भवेत्सर्वं रसिकालिंगनेन च ॥ 8 ॥

4.42.s:
sahasrasundarīkāntaṃ kāmaśāstra viśāradam ..
kiṃkaraṃ kuru māṃ kānte parityakṣyāmi tā api ..9..
4.42.d:
सहस्रसुन्दरीकान्तं कामशास्त्र विशारदम् ॥
किंकरं कुरु मां कान्ते परित्यक्ष्यामि ता अपि ॥9॥

4.42.s:
nirjale nirjane ramye śaileśaile nadenade ..
puṣpodyāne puṣpite ca sugandhipuṣpavāyunā ..4.42.10..
4.42.d:
निर्जले निर्जने रम्ये शैलेशैले नदेनदे ॥
पुष्पोद्याने पुष्पिते च सुगन्धिपुष्पवायुना ॥4.42.10॥

4.42.s:
malaye candanāraṇye cārucandanavāyunā ..
vihariṣyāmi kāmena kāminyā ca tvayā saha..11..
4.42.d:
मलये चन्दनारण्ये चारुचन्दनवायुना ॥
विहरिष्यामि कामेन कामिन्या च त्वया सह॥11॥

4.42.s:
kāmajvareṇa dagdhāyāḥ śāṃtiṃ kartumahaṃ kṣamaḥ ..
viharasva mayā sārddhaṃ janmedaṃ saphalaṃ kuru ..12..
4.42.d:
कामज्वरेण दग्धायाः शांतिं कर्तुमहं क्षमः ॥
विहरस्व मया सार्द्धं जन्मेदं सफलं कुरु ॥12॥

4.42.s:
ityevamuktavaṃtaṃ taṃ svarathādavaruhya ca ..
grahītumutsukaṃ hastaṃ tamuvāca pativratā .. 13 ..
4.42.d:
इत्येवमुक्तवंतं तं स्वरथादवरुह्य च ॥
ग्रहीतुमुत्सुकं हस्तं तमुवाच पतिव्रता ॥ 13 ॥

4.42.s:
padmovāca ..
dūraṃ gaccha gaccha dūraṃ pāpiṣṭha bhūmipādhama ..
māṃ cetpaśyasi kāmena sadyo bhasma bhaviṣyasi .. 14 ..
4.42.d:
पद्मोवाच ॥
दूरं गच्छ गच्छ दूरं पापिष्ठ भूमिपाधम ॥
मां चेत्पश्यसि कामेन सद्यो भस्म भविष्यसि ॥ 14 ॥

4.42.s:
pippalādaṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ tapasā pūtavigraham..
vihāya tvāṃ bhajiṣyāmi strījitaṃ ratilaṃpaṭam ..15..
4.42.d:
पिप्पलादं मुनिश्रेष्ठं तपसा पूतविग्रहम्॥
विहाय त्वां भजिष्यामि स्त्रीजितं रतिलंपटम् ॥15॥

4.42.s:
strījitasparśamātreṇa sarvapuṇyaṃ praṇaśyati ..
na bhūmau pātakī pāpātpāpināṃ strījitātparaḥ .. 16 ..
4.42.d:
स्त्रीजितस्पर्शमात्रेण सर्वपुण्यं प्रणश्यति ॥
न भूमौ पातकी पापात्पापिनां स्त्रीजितात्परः ॥ 16 ॥

4.42.s:
māṃ mātaraṃ ca strībhāvaṃ kṛtvā yena bravīṣi ca ..
bhaviṣyati kṣayastena kālena mama śāpataḥ .. 17 ..
4.42.d:
मां मातरं च स्त्रीभावं कृत्वा येन ब्रवीषि च ॥
भविष्यति क्षयस्तेन कालेन मम शापतः ॥ 17 ॥

4.42.s:
śrutvā dharmaḥ satīśāpaṃ nṛpamūrtiṃ vihāya ca ..
dhṛtvā svamūrtiṃ deveśaḥ kaṃpamāna uvāca tām .. 18 ..
4.42.d:
श्रुत्वा धर्मः सतीशापं नृपमूर्तिं विहाय च ॥
धृत्वा स्वमूर्तिं देवेशः कंपमान उवाच ताम् ॥ 18 ॥

4.42.s:
dharma uvāca ..
mātarjānīhi māṃ dharmaṃ dharmajñānāṃ gurorgurum ..
parastrīmātṛbuddhiṃ ca kurvantaṃ saṃtataṃ sati .. 19 ..
4.42.d:
धर्म उवाच ॥
मातर्जानीहि मां धर्मं धर्मज्ञानां गुरोर्गुरुम् ॥
परस्त्रीमातृबुद्धिं च कुर्वन्तं संततं सति ॥ 19 ॥

4.42.s:
ahaṃ tavāṃtarvijñātumāgatastava sannidhim ..
yuṣmākaṃ ca mano jāne tathāpi daivabodhitaḥ .. 4.42.20 ..
4.42.d:
अहं तवांतर्विज्ञातुमागतस्तव सन्निधिम् ॥
युष्माकं च मनो जाने तथापि दैवबोधितः ॥ 4.42.20 ॥

4.42.s:
kṛtaṃ me damanaṃ sādhvi na viruddhaṃ yathocitam ..
śāstiḥ samutpathasthānāmīśvareṇa vinirmitā .. 21 ..
4.42.d:
कृतं मे दमनं साध्वि न विरुद्धं यथोचितम् ॥
शास्तिः समुत्पथस्थानामीश्वरेण विनिर्मिता ॥ 21 ॥

4.42.s:
dharmaṃ svadharmaṃ vijñātuṃ kālaṃ kalayituṃ kṣamaḥ ..
vidhātāraṃ saṃvidhātuṃ tasmai kṛṣṇāya te namaḥ ..22..
4.42.d:
धर्मं स्वधर्मं विज्ञातुं कालं कलयितुं क्षमः ॥
विधातारं संविधातुं तस्मै कृष्णाय ते नमः ॥22॥

4.42.s:
saṃhartuṃ yaḥ kṣamaḥ kāle saṃhartāraṃ bhavaṃ vibhuḥ ..
sraṣṭāraṃ līlayā sraṣṭuṃ tasmai kṛṣṇāya te namaḥ .. 23 ..
4.42.d:
संहर्तुं यः क्षमः काले संहर्तारं भवं विभुः ॥
स्रष्टारं लीलया स्रष्टुं तस्मै कृष्णाय ते नमः ॥ 23 ॥

4.42.s:
śatruṃ vidhātuṃ mitraṃ ca suprītiṃ kalahaṃ kṣamaḥ ..
sraṣṭuṃ naṣṭam tadevaṃ ca tasmai kṛṣṇāya te namaḥ .. 24 ..
4.42.d:
शत्रुं विधातुं मित्रं च सुप्रीतिं कलहं क्षमः ॥
स्रष्टुं नष्टम् तदेवं च तस्मै कृष्णाय ते नमः ॥ 24 ॥

4.42.s:
śāpaṃ pradātuṃ sarvāśca sukhaduḥkhavarānkṣamaḥ ..
saṃpadaṃ vipadaṃ yo hi tasmai kṛṣṇāya te namaḥ .. 25 ..
4.42.d:
शापं प्रदातुं सर्वाश्च सुखदुःखवरान्क्षमः ॥
संपदं विपदं यो हि तस्मै कृष्णाय ते नमः ॥ 25 ॥

4.42.s:
prakṛtirnirmitā yena mahāviṣṇuśca nirmitaḥ ..
brahmaviṣṇumaheśādyāstasmai kṛṣṇāya te namaḥ .. 26 ..
4.42.d:
प्रकृतिर्निर्मिता येन महाविष्णुश्च निर्मितः ॥
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशाद्यास्तस्मै कृष्णाय ते नमः ॥ 26 ॥

4.42.s:
yena śuklīkṛtaṃ kṣīraṃ jalaṃ śītaṃ kṛtaṃ purā ..
dāhīkṛto hutāśaśca tasmai kṛṣṇāya te namaḥ .. 27 ..
4.42.d:
येन शुक्लीकृतं क्षीरं जलं शीतं कृतं पुरा ॥
दाहीकृतो हुताशश्च तस्मै कृष्णाय ते नमः ॥ 27 ॥

4.42.s:
atitejaḥ samutthāya tejorūpāya mūrttaye ..
guṇaśreṣṭhanirguṇāya tasmai kṛṣṇāya te namaḥ ..28..
4.42.d:
अतितेजः समुत्थाय तेजोरूपाय मूर्त्तये ॥
गुणश्रेष्ठनिर्गुणाय तस्मै कृष्णाय ते नमः ॥28॥

4.42.s:
sarvasmai sarvabījāya sarveṣāmantarātmane..
sarvabaṃdhusvarūpāya tasmai kṛṣṇāya te namaḥ .. 29 ..
4.42.d:
सर्वस्मै सर्वबीजाय सर्वेषामन्तरात्मने॥
सर्वबंधुस्वरूपाय तस्मै कृष्णाय ते नमः ॥ 29 ॥

4.42.s:
ityuktvā puratastasyāstasthau dharmo jagadguruḥ ..
sā sādhvī taṃ ca vijñāya sahasovāca parvata .. 4.42.30 ..
4.42.d:
इत्युक्त्वा पुरतस्तस्यास्तस्थौ धर्मो जगद्गुरुः ॥
सा साध्वी तं च विज्ञाय सहसोवाच पर्वत ॥ 4.42.30 ॥

4.42.s:
padmovāca ..
tvameva dharmaḥ sarveṣāṃ sākṣī ca sarvakarmaṇām ..
sarvāṃtareṣu sarvātmā sarvajñaḥ sarvatattvavit .. 31 ..
4.42.d:
पद्मोवाच ॥
त्वमेव धर्मः सर्वेषां साक्षी च सर्वकर्मणाम् ॥
सर्वांतरेषु सर्वात्मा सर्वज्ञः सर्वतत्त्ववित् ॥ 31 ॥

4.42.s:
kathaṃ mano me vijñātuṃ viḍaṃbayasi kiṃkarīm ..
yatkṛtaṃ tvatkṛte brahmannaparādho babhūva me ..32..
4.42.d:
कथं मनो मे विज्ञातुं विडंबयसि किंकरीम् ॥
यत्कृतं त्वत्कृते ब्रह्मन्नपराधो बभूव मे ॥32॥

4.42.s:
tvaṃ ca śapto mayā'jñānātstrīsvabhāvātkrudhā vibho ..
kā vyavasthā bhavettasya cintayāmīti sāṃpratam .. 33 ..
4.42.d:
त्वं च शप्तो मयाऽज्ञानात्स्त्रीस्वभावात्क्रुधा विभो ॥
का व्यवस्था भवेत्तस्य चिन्तयामीति सांप्रतम् ॥ 33 ॥

4.42.s:
ākāśo'sau diśaḥ sarvā yadi naśyanti vāyavaḥ ..
tathāpi sādhvīśāpastu na naśyati kadācana .. 34 ..
4.42.d:
आकाशोऽसौ दिशः सर्वा यदि नश्यन्ति वायवः ॥
तथापि साध्वीशापस्तु न नश्यति कदाचन ॥ 34 ॥

4.42.s:
tvaṃ ca naṣṭo bhavasi cetsṛṣṭināśo bhavettadā ..
iti kartavyatāmūḍhā tathāpi tvāṃ vadāmyaham .. 35 ..
4.42.d:
त्वं च नष्टो भवसि चेत्सृष्टिनाशो भवेत्तदा ॥
इति कर्तव्यतामूढा तथापि त्वां वदाम्यहम् ॥ 35 ॥

4.42.s:
satye pūrṇaścatuṣpādaiḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ yathā śaśī ..
virājase devarāja sarvakālaṃ divāniśam .. 36 ..
4.42.d:
सत्ये पूर्णश्चतुष्पादैः पौर्णमास्यां यथा शशी ॥
विराजसे देवराज सर्वकालं दिवानिशम् ॥ 36 ॥

4.42.s:
pādakṣayaśca tretāyāṃ bhagavanbhavitā tava ..
pādau parau dvāpare ca tṛtīyaśca kalau vibho .. 37 ..
4.42.d:
पादक्षयश्च त्रेतायां भगवन्भविता तव ॥
पादौ परौ द्वापरे च तृतीयश्च कलौ विभो ॥ 37 ॥

4.42.s:
kaliśeṣe śeṣapādastavācchanno bhaviṣyati ..
punaḥ satye samāyāte paripūrṇo bhaviṣyasi .. 38 ..
4.42.d:
कलिशेषे शेषपादस्तवाच्छन्नो भविष्यति ॥
पुनः सत्ये समायाते परिपूर्णो भविष्यसि ॥ 38 ॥

4.42.s:
satye sarvavyāpakastvaṃ tadanyeṣu ca kutracit ..
yatra sthānaṃ tavādhāro vadāmi śrūyatāṃ vibho ..39 ..
4.42.d:
सत्ये सर्वव्यापकस्त्वं तदन्येषु च कुत्रचित् ॥
यत्र स्थानं तवाधारो वदामि श्रूयतां विभो ॥39 ॥

4.42.s:
vaiṣṇaveṣu ca sarveṣu yatiṣu brahmacāriṣu ..
pativratāsu prājñeṣu vānaprastheṣu bhikṣuṣu .. 4.42.40 ..
4.42.d:
वैष्णवेषु च सर्वेषु यतिषु ब्रह्मचारिषु ॥
पतिव्रतासु प्राज्ञेषु वानप्रस्थेषु भिक्षुषु ॥ 4.42.40 ॥

4.42.s:
nṛpeṣu dharmaśīleṣu satsu sadvaiśyajātiṣu ..
dvijaseviṣu śūdreṣu satsaṃsargasthiteṣu ca .. 41..
4.42.d:
नृपेषु धर्मशीलेषु सत्सु सद्वैश्यजातिषु ॥
द्विजसेविषु शूद्रेषु सत्संसर्गस्थितेषु च ॥ 41॥

4.42.s:
eṣu tvaṃ satataṃ pūrṇo dharmarāja virājase ..
yugeyuge tadādhārā yatra puṇyatamā janāḥ .. 42 ..
4.42.d:
एषु त्वं सततं पूर्णो धर्मराज विराजसे ॥
युगेयुगे तदाधारा यत्र पुण्यतमा जनाः ॥ 42 ॥

4.42.s:
aśvatthavaṭabilveṣu tulasīcaṃdaneṣu ca ..
dīkṣāparīkṣāśapathagoṣṭhagoṣpadabhūmiṣu ..43..
4.42.d:
अश्वत्थवटबिल्वेषु तुलसीचंदनेषु च ॥
दीक्षापरीक्षाशपथगोष्ठगोष्पदभूमिषु ॥43॥

4.42.s:
vivāheṣu ca puṣpeṣu vidyamāno'si śākhiṣu ..
devālayeṣu tīrtheṣu satāṃ śaśvadgṛheṣu ca .. 44 ..
4.42.d:
विवाहेषु च पुष्पेषु विद्यमानोऽसि शाखिषु ॥
देवालयेषु तीर्थेषु सतां शश्वद्गृहेषु च ॥ 44 ॥

4.42.s:
vedavedāṃgaśravaṇe jaleṣu ca sabhāsu ca .
śrīkṛṣṇaguṇanāmokta śrutigītasthaleṣu ca .. 45 ..
4.42.d:
वेदवेदांगश्रवणे जलेषु च सभासु च ।
श्रीकृष्णगुणनामोक्त श्रुतिगीतस्थलेषु च ॥ 45 ॥

4.42.s:
vratapūjātaponyāyayajñasākṣisthaleṣu ca ..
gavāṃ gṛheṣu goṣveva vidyamāno hi paśyasi .. 46 ..
4.42.d:
व्रतपूजातपोन्याययज्ञसाक्षिस्थलेषु च ॥
गवां गृहेषु गोष्वेव विद्यमानो हि पश्यसि ॥ 46 ॥

4.42.s:
kṛśatā tena bhavitā dharma teṣu sthaleṣu ca ..
etadanyeṣu kṛśatā yadagamyaṃ ca tacchṛṇu .. 47 ..
4.42.d:
कृशता तेन भविता धर्म तेषु स्थलेषु च ॥
एतदन्येषु कृशता यदगम्यं च तच्छृणु ॥ 47 ॥

4.42.s:
puṃścalīṣu ca sarvāsu gṛheṣu naraghātinām ..
naraghātiṣu nīceṣu mūrkheṣu ca khaleṣu ca .. 48 ..
4.42.d:
पुंश्चलीषु च सर्वासु गृहेषु नरघातिनाम् ॥
नरघातिषु नीचेषु मूर्खेषु च खलेषु च ॥ 48 ॥

4.42.s:
devatāguruvipreṣṭapālyānāṃ dhanahāriṣu ..
asannareṣu dhūrteṣu caureṣu ratibhūmiṣu ..49..
4.42.d:
देवतागुरुविप्रेष्टपाल्यानां धनहारिषु ॥
असन्नरेषु धूर्तेषु चौरेषु रतिभूमिषु ॥49॥

4.42.s:
durodarasurāpānakalahānāṃ sthaleṣu ca ..
śālagrāmasādhutīrthapurāṇarahiteṣu ca .. 4.42.50 ..
4.42.d:
दुरोदरसुरापानकलहानां स्थलेषु च ॥
शालग्रामसाधुतीर्थपुराणरहितेषु च ॥ 4.42.50 ॥

4.42.s:
dasyusneheṣu vādeṣu tālacchāyāsu garviṣu..
asijīvimaṣījīvidevalagrāmayājiṣu ..51..
4.42.d:
दस्युस्नेहेषु वादेषु तालच्छायासु गर्विषु॥
असिजीविमषीजीविदेवलग्रामयाजिषु ॥51॥
4.42.m:
in friendships with robbers, in disputes, in the shade of palm trees, among the arrogant,
among professional soldiers, professional scribes, temple-priests, and priests for whole villages,

4.42.s:
vṛṣavāhasvarṇakārajīvahiṃsopajīviṣu ..
bhartṛniṃditanārīṣu strījiteṣu ca puṃsu ca .. 52 ..
4.42.d:
वृषवाहस्वर्णकारजीवहिंसोपजीविषु ॥
भर्तृनिंदितनारीषु स्त्रीजितेषु च पुंसु च ॥ 52 ॥
4.42.m:
among those who ride bulls, goldsmiths, and those who subsist on killing living beings,
among women who disparage their husbands, and among men subjugated by women,

4.42.s:
dīkṣāsaṃdhyāviṣṇubhaktivihīneṣu dvijeṣu ca ..
svāṃgakanyāvikrayiṣu svayoṣidvikrayeṣvatha .. 53 ..
4.42.d:
दीक्षासंध्याविष्णुभक्तिविहीनेषु द्विजेषु च ॥
स्वांगकन्याविक्रयिषु स्वयोषिद्विक्रयेष्वथ ॥ 53 ॥
4.42.m:
and among twice-born men devoid of initiation, the twilight prayer, and devotion to Viṣṇu,
among those who sell their own bodies or daughters, and also in sales of their own wives,

4.42.s:
śālagrāmasuragraṃthabhūmivikrayiṣu prabho ..
mitradohikṛtaghneṣu satyaviśvāsaghātiṣu .. 54 ..
4.42.d:
शालग्रामसुरग्रंथभूमिविक्रयिषु प्रभो ॥
मित्रदोहिकृतघ्नेषु सत्यविश्वासघातिषु ॥ 54 ॥
4.42.m:
among those who sell a Śāligrāma, sacred scriptures, or land, O lord,
among betrayers of friends, the ungrateful, and violators of truth and trust,

4.42.s:
śaraṇāgatadīneṣu cāśritaghneṣu nṛṣvapi ..
śaśvanmithyoktiśīleṣu tathā sīmāpahāriṣu .. 55 ..
4.42.d:
शरणागतदीनेषु चाश्रितघ्नेषु नृष्वपि ॥
शश्वन्मिथ्योक्तिशीलेषु तथा सीमापहारिषु ॥ 55 ॥
4.42.m:
even among men who kill those who have surrendered, the wretched, and dependents,
among those habitually telling lies, and likewise those who steal boundary-lands,

4.42.s:
kāmātkrodhāttathā lobhānmithyāsākṣipravādiṣu ..
puṇyakarmavihīneṣu puṇyakarmavirodhiṣu .. 56 ..
4.42.d:
कामात्क्रोधात्तथा लोभान्मिथ्यासाक्षिप्रवादिषु ॥
पुण्यकर्मविहीनेषु पुण्यकर्मविरोधिषु ॥ 56 ॥
4.42.m:
among those who give false testimony out of lust, anger, or greed,
among those devoid of meritorious deeds and those who oppose meritorious deeds—

4.42.s:
sthātumeteṣu nindyeṣu nādhikārastava prabho ..
mamāpi vacanaṃ satyaṃ babhūva tatkṣaṇaṃ tava .. 57 ..
4.42.d:
स्थातुमेतेषु निन्द्येषु नाधिकारस्तव प्रभो ॥
ममापि वचनं सत्यं बभूव तत्क्षणं तव ॥ 57 ॥
4.42.m:
you have no right, O lord, to reside among these contemptible ones.
Even my word has instantly come true for you.

4.42.s:
yāsyāmi patisevāyai gaccha tāta svamandiram ..
ityevaṃvādinīṃ sādhvīmuvāca vidhinandanaḥ ..
prasannavadanaḥ śrīmānatīva vinayaṃ vacaḥ .. 58 ..
4.42.d:
यास्यामि पतिसेवायै गच्छ तात स्वमन्दिरम् ॥
इत्येवंवादिनीं साध्वीमुवाच विधिनन्दनः ॥
प्रसन्नवदनः श्रीमानतीव विनयं वचः ॥ 58 ॥
4.42.m:
I shall go to serve my husband; go, father, to your own abode."
To the virtuous woman speaking thus, the son of Brahmā,
resplendent and with a joyful countenance, spoke words full of humility:

4.42.s:
dharma uvāca ..
dhanyā'si patibhaktā'si svasti te'stu ca saṃtatam .. 59 ..
4.42.d:
धर्म उवाच ॥
धन्याऽसि पतिभक्ताऽसि स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु च संततम् ॥ 59 ॥
4.42.m: "Blessed are you, devoted to your husband! May constant well-being be yours.

4.42.s:
varaṃ gṛhāṇa dāsyāmi matparitrāṇakāriṇi ..
yuvā bhavatu bhartā te ratiśūraśca kanyake .. .. 4.42.60 ..
4.42.d:
वरं गृहाण दास्यामि मत्परित्राणकारिणि ॥
युवा भवतु भर्ता ते रतिशूरश्च कन्यके ॥ ॥ 4.42.60 ॥
4.42.m:
Accept a boon; I shall grant it, O you who rescued me!
May your husband become young and skilled in lovemaking, O maiden!

4.42.s:
rūpavānguṇavānsādhvi saṃtataṃ sthirayauvanaḥ ..
paramaiśvaryasaṃyuktā tvaṃ bhava sthirayauvanā .. 61 ..
4.42.d:
रूपवान्गुणवान्साध्वि संततं स्थिरयौवनः ॥
परमैश्वर्यसंयुक्ता त्वं भव स्थिरयौवना ॥ 61 ॥
4.42.m:
Handsome, virtuous, O virtuous lady, and constantly endowed with unaging youth;
and you, endowed with supreme opulence, be endowed with unaging youth!

4.42.s:
cirajīvī bhavatu sa mārkaṇḍeyātparaḥ sute ..
kuberāddhanavāṃścaiva śakrādaiśvaryavānapi .. 62 ..
4.42.d:
चिरजीवी भवतु स मार्कण्डेयात्परः सुते ॥
कुबेराद्धनवांश्चैव शक्रादैश्वर्यवानपि ॥ 62 ॥
4.42.m:
May he live long, surpassing Mārkaṇḍeya, O daughter,
richer even than Kubera, and endowed with more sovereignty than Indra;

4.42.s:
viṣṇubhaktaḥ śivasamaḥ siddhastu kapilātparaḥ ..
svāmisaubhāgyasaṃyuktā bhava tvaṃ jīvanāvadhi .. 63 ..
4.42.d:
विष्णुभक्तः शिवसमः सिद्धस्तु कपिलात्परः ॥
स्वामिसौभाग्यसंयुक्ता भव त्वं जीवनावधि ॥ 63 ॥
4.42.m:
a devotee of Viṣṇu, equal to Śiva, and accomplished beyond Kapila!
May you be endowed with your husband's favour for the duration of your life!

4.42.s:
gṛhā bhavantu te sādhvi kuberabhavanādhikāḥ ..
mātā tvaṃ daśaputrāṇāṃ guṇināṃ cirajīvinām .. .. 64 ..
4.42.d:
गृहा भवन्तु ते साध्वि कुबेरभवनाधिकाः ॥
माता त्वं दशपुत्राणां गुणिनां चिरजीविनाम् ॥ ॥ 64 ॥
4.42.m:
May your homes, O virtuous woman, surpass the mansion of Kubera;
and you, the mother of ten virtuous, long-lived sons,

4.42.s:
svabharturadhikānāṃ ca bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ ..
ityevamuktvā saṃtasthau dharmarājaśca parvata ..69..
4.42.d:
स्वभर्तुरधिकानां च भविष्यसि न संशयः ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा संतस्थौ धर्मराजश्च पर्वत ॥69॥
4.42.m:
who will even surpass their father—of this there is no doubt."
Having spoken thus, O Mountain, Dharmarāja paused.

4.42.s:
sā taṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya praṇamya svagṛhaṃ yayau ..
dharmastāmāśiṣaṃ yuktvā jagāma nijamandiram .. 66 ..
4.42.d:
सा तं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य प्रणम्य स्वगृहं ययौ ॥
धर्मस्तामाशिषं युक्त्वा जगाम निजमन्दिरम् ॥ 66 ॥
4.42.m:
Having circumambulated him and bowed, she went to her own house.
Having bestowed that blessing upon her, Dharma went to his own abode.

4.42.s:
pativratāṃ praśaśaṃsa pratisaṃsadi saṃsadi ..
sā reme svāminā sārddhaṃ yūnā rahasi saṃtatam .. 67 ..
4.42.d:
पतिव्रतां प्रशशंस प्रतिसंसदि संसदि ॥
सा रेमे स्वामिना सार्द्धं यूना रहसि संततम् ॥ 67 ॥
4.42.m:
He praised the devoted wife in assembly after assembly.
She constantly rejoiced in secret with her youthful husband.

4.42.s:
paścādbabhūva satputrā tadbharturadhikā guṇaiḥ ..
śailendra kathitaṃ sarvamitihāsaṃ purātanam .. 68 ..
4.42.d:
पश्चाद्बभूव सत्पुत्रा तद्भर्तुरधिका गुणैः ॥
शैलेन्द्र कथितं सर्वमितिहासं पुरातनम् ॥ 68 ॥
4.42.m:
Afterwards she bore noble sons who surpassed their father in virtues.
O king of mountains, this entire ancient history has been told to you.

4.42.s:
dattvā'naraṇyaḥ svasutāṃ rarakṣa sarvasaṃpadam ..
tvameva kanyakāṃ dattvā sarveṣāmīśvarāya ca ..69..
4.42.d:
दत्त्वाऽनरण्यः स्वसुतां ररक्ष सर्वसंपदम् ॥
त्वमेव कन्यकां दत्त्वा सर्वेषामीश्वराय च ॥69॥
4.42.m:
By giving his daughter, Anaraṇya protected all his prosperity.
Do you likewise, having given your daughter to the Lord of all,

4.42.s:
rakṣa sarvabandhuvargānātmanaḥ sarvasaṃpadam ..
saptāhe samatīte ca durlabhe'tiśubhe kṣaṇe ..4.42.70..
4.42.d:
रक्ष सर्वबन्धुवर्गानात्मनः सर्वसंपदम् ॥
सप्ताहे समतीते च दुर्लभेऽतिशुभे क्षणे ॥4.42.70॥
4.42.m:
protect all your kinsmen and all your wealth!
When seven days have passed, at a rare and most auspicious moment,

4.42.s:
lagnādhipe ca lagnasthe candre svatanayānvite ..
modate rohiṇīyukte viśuddhe candratārake .. 71 ..
4.42.d:
लग्नाधिपे च लग्नस्थे चन्द्रे स्वतनयान्विते ॥
मोदते रोहिणीयुक्ते विशुद्धे चन्द्रतारके ॥ 71 ॥
4.42.m:
when the lord of the ascendant is in the ascendant, and the Moon is with Mercury,
delighting in conjunction with Rohiṇī, with the Moon and stars pure,

4.42.s:
mārgaśīrṣe candravāre sarvadoṣavivarjite ..
sarvasadgrahasaṃdṛṣṭe hyasadgrahavivarjite .. 72 ..
4.42.d:
मार्गशीर्षे चन्द्रवारे सर्वदोषविवर्जिते ॥
सर्वसद्ग्रहसंदृष्टे ह्यसद्ग्रहविवर्जिते ॥ 72 ॥
4.42.m:
in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, on a Monday free of all blemishes,
aspected by all beneficent planets and indeed devoid of malefics,

4.42.s:
sadapatyaprade'tīva patisaubhāgyadāyini ..
avaidhavyaprade saukhyaprade janmani janmani .. 73 ..
4.42.d:
सदपत्यप्रदेऽतीव पतिसौभाग्यदायिनि ॥
अवैधव्यप्रदे सौख्यप्रदे जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥ 73 ॥
4.42.m:
bestowing noble offspring, granting great fortune with a husband,
preventing widowhood, bestowing happiness birth after birth,

4.42.s:
atyantapremāvicchedapradāyini parātpare ..
kanyāṃ pradāya devāya tvaṃ kṛtī bhava parvata .. 74 ..
4.42.d:
अत्यन्तप्रेमाविच्छेदप्रदायिनि परात्परे ॥
कन्यां प्रदाय देवाय त्वं कृती भव पर्वत ॥ 74 ॥
4.42.m:
granting unsevered, supreme love, beyond the highest—
give your maiden to the god, O mountain, and be fulfilled!

4.42.s:
jagadambāṃ jagatpitre mūlaprakṛtimīśvarīm ..
tejaḥsvarūpāṃ sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ devapūjitām .. 79 ..
4.42.d:
जगदम्बां जगत्पित्रे मूलप्रकृतिमीश्वरीम् ॥
तेजःस्वरूपां सर्वेषां देवानां देवपूजिताम् ॥ 79 ॥
4.42.m:
[Give] the Mother of the Universe to the Father of the Universe, Mūlaprakṛti, the Sovereign Goddess,
whose essence is splendor, worshipped by the gods among all deities.

4.42.s:
āvirbhūtā purā kalpe devānāṃ rakṣaṇāya ca ..
tejorāśiḥ suraughāṇāṃ prajvalanto diśo daśa .. 76 ..
4.42.d:
आविर्भूता पुरा कल्पे देवानां रक्षणाय च ॥
तेजोराशिः सुरौघाणां प्रज्वलन्तो दिशो दश ॥ 76 ॥
4.42.m:
She manifested in a former kalpa for the protection of the gods;
the mass of splendor of the hosts of gods, blazing forth in the ten directions,

4.42.s:
asyāḥ svatejasā daityāḥ keciddagdhāḥ palāyitāḥ ..
kecidbabhūvuḥ śailendra bhasmībhūtāśca bhūtale .. 77 ..
4.42.d:
अस्याः स्वतेजसा दैत्याः केचिद्दग्धाः पलायिताः ॥
केचिद्बभूवुः शैलेन्द्र भस्मीभूताश्च भूतले ॥ 77 ॥
4.42.m:
by her own radiance some Daityas were burned, others fled;
some, O lord of mountains, were turned to ashes on the surface of the earth;

4.42.s:
bilaṃ praviviśuḥ kecinmūrcchāṃ prāpuśca kecana ..
keciddante tṛṇaṃ kṛtvā jagmuḥ śaraṇamīśvarīm .. 78 ..
4.42.d:
बिलं प्रविविशुः केचिन्मूर्च्छां प्रापुश्च केचन ॥
केचिद्दन्ते तृणं कृत्वा जग्मुः शरणमीश्वरीम् ॥ 78 ॥
4.42.m:
some entered caves, and some fell into a swoon;
some, placing grass between their teeth, took refuge in the Sovereign Goddess;

4.42.s:
keciccikṣipurastrāṇi stambhitā api kecana ..
kecicciraṃ raṇaṃ kṛtvā yayuḥ svargamanāmayam .. 79 ..
4.42.d:
केचिच्चिक्षिपुरस्त्राणि स्तम्भिता अपि केचन ॥
केचिच्चिरं रणं कृत्वा ययुः स्वर्गमनामयम् ॥ 79 ॥
4.42.m:
some hurled weapons, and yet others were paralyzed;
some, having fought for a long time, went to painless heaven.

4.42.s:
niḥśatravo babhūvuste surā asyāḥ prasādataḥ ..
kṛṣṇājñayā sā kalpānte dakṣakanyā babhūva ha .. 4.42.80 ..
4.42.d:
निःशत्रवो बभूवुस्ते सुरा अस्याः प्रसादतः ॥
कृष्णाज्ञया सा कल्पान्ते दक्षकन्या बभूव ह ॥ 4.42.80 ॥
4.42.m:
Those gods became free of enemies by her grace.
By Kṛṣṇa's command, she became Dakṣa's daughter at the end of the kalpa.

4.42.s:
dakṣaśca vidhivaddevīṃ pradadau śūlapāṇaye ..
daivena matpituryajñe sahasā surasaṃsadi .. 81 ..
4.42.d:
दक्षश्च विधिवद्देवीं प्रददौ शूलपाणये ॥
दैवेन मत्पितुर्यज्ञे सहसा सुरसंसदि ॥ 81 ॥
4.42.m:
And Dakṣa gave the goddess in marriage to the trident-bearer according to rule.
By fate, at my father's sacrifice, suddenly in the assembly of the gods,

4.42.s:
babhūva kalahaḥ śaila tena śūlabhṛtā mahān ..
brahmāṇaṃ ca namaskṛtya yayau ruṣṭastrilocanaḥ .. 82 ..
4.42.d:
बभूव कलहः शैल तेन शूलभृता महान् ॥
ब्रह्माणं च नमस्कृत्य ययौ रुष्टस्त्रिलोचनः ॥ 82 ॥
4.42.m:
a great quarrel arose, O mountain, with that trident-bearer.
Bowing to Brahmā, the three-eyed one departed in anger.

4.42.s:
dakṣaśca sagaṇo ruṣṭaḥ prayayau svālayaṃ tadā ..
kopātsaṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro dakṣo yajñaṃ cakāra ha .. 83 ..
4.42.d:
दक्षश्च सगणो रुष्टः प्रययौ स्वालयं तदा ॥
कोपात्संभृतसंभारो दक्षो यज्ञं चकार ह ॥ 83 ॥
4.42.m:
And Dakṣa too, enraged, then went to his own abode with his retinue.
Gathering materials out of anger, Dakṣa performed a sacrifice;

4.42.s:
na dadau yajñabhāgaṃ ca mātsaryācchūlapāṇaye ..
dṛṣṭvā satī prakupitā janakaṃ raktalocanā .. 84 ..
4.42.d:
न ददौ यज्ञभागं च मात्सर्याच्छूलपाणये ॥
दृष्ट्वा सती प्रकुपिता जनकं रक्तलोचना ॥ 84 ॥
4.42.m:
and out of malice he did not give a sacrificial share to the trident-bearer.
Seeing [this], Satī, greatly enraged, with red eyes,

4.42.s:
nirbhartsya ca bahutaraṃ hṛdayena vidūyatā ..
yajñasthānātsamutthāya jagāma māturantikam .. 85 ..
4.42.d:
निर्भर्त्स्य च बहुतरं हृदयेन विदूयता ॥
यज्ञस्थानात्समुत्थाय जगाम मातुरन्तिकम् ॥ 85 ॥
4.42.m:
rebuked her father severely with an agonizing heart,
and rising from the place of sacrifice, she went to her mother's presence.

4.42.s:
bhaviṣyaṃ kathayāmāsa trikālajñā parātparā ..
yajñabhaṅgādikaṃ vā'pi svapituśca parābhavam .. 86 ..
4.42.d:
भविष्यं कथयामास त्रिकालज्ञा परात्परा ॥
यज्ञभङ्गादिकं वाऽपि स्वपितुश्च पराभवम् ॥ 86 ॥
4.42.m:
Knowing the three times, beyond the highest, she told the future:
the destruction of the sacrifice and the humiliation of her own father,

4.42.s:
palāyanaṃ ca devānāṃ yajñasthānādgirīśvaram ..
munīnāmṛtvijāṃ caiva parvatānāṃ tathaiva ca .. 87 ..
4.42.d:
पलायनं च देवानां यज्ञस्थानाद्गिरीश्वरम् ॥
मुनीनामृत्विजां चैव पर्वतानां तथैव च ॥ 87 ॥
4.42.m:
and the flight of the gods, O lord of mountains, from the sacrificial arena,
and of the sages, the priests, and likewise of the mountains,

4.42.s:
jayaṃ śaṃkarasainyānāṃ svātmano mṛtyumeva ca ..
śokātparyaṭanaṃ bharturvirahāturacetasā .. 88 ..
4.42.d:
जयं शंकरसैन्यानां स्वात्मनो मृत्युमेव च ॥
शोकात्पर्यटनं भर्तुर्विरहातुरचेतसा ॥ 88 ॥
4.42.m:
the victory of Śaṅkara's armies, and indeed her own death,
her husband's wandering in grief with a mind distressed by separation,

4.42.s:
nirmāṇaṃ netrarasaḥ prabodhaṃ ca janārdanāt ..
mūrtibhedātpunaḥ prāptiṃ vihāraṃ tasya tatsamam ..89..
4.42.d:
निर्माणं नेत्ररसः प्रबोधं च जनार्दनात् ॥
मूर्तिभेदात्पुनः प्राप्तिं विहारं तस्य तत्समम् ॥89॥
4.42.m:
the making of tears of affection and his awakening by Janārdana,
her attainment [of him] again in a different form, and his sporting equal to that [before].

4.42.s:
aparaṃ bhavitavyaṃ ca sarvamuktvā jagāma sā ..
svamātrā bhaginībhiśca pratiṣiddhā ca duḥkhitā .. 4.42.90 ..
4.42.d:
अपरं भवितव्यं च सर्वमुक्त्वा जगाम सा ॥
स्वमात्रा भगिनीभिश्च प्रतिषिद्धा च दुःखिता ॥ 4.42.90 ॥
4.42.m:
Having spoken of all else that was to happen, she departed,
forbidden by her mother and sisters, and sorrowful.

4.42.s:
babhūvādarśanā yogātsarvāsāṃ siddhiyoginī ..
gatvā sā jāhnavītīraṃ smṛtvā saṃpūjya śaṃkaram .. 91 ..
4.42.d:
बभूवादर्शना योगात्सर्वासां सिद्धियोगिनी ॥
गत्वा सा जाह्नवीतीरं स्मृत्वा संपूज्य शंकरम् ॥ 91 ॥
4.42.m:
The accomplished yoginī vanished from the sight of all through yoga;
having gone to the bank of the Jāhnavī, having remembered and worshipped Śaṅkara,

4.42.s:
smṛtvā taccaraṇāmbhojaṃ dehaṃ tatyāja sundarī ..
gandhamādanadroṇīsthaṃ śarīraṃ praviveśa ha .. 92 ..
4.42.d:
स्मृत्वा तच्चरणाम्भोजं देहं तत्याज सुन्दरी ॥
गन्धमादनद्रोणीस्थं शरीरं प्रविवेश ह ॥ 92 ॥
4.42.m:
having remembered his lotus feet, the beautiful woman abandoned her body.
She entered the body lying in the valley of Mount Gandhamādana,

4.42.s:
saṃjahāra purā yena daityānāmakhilaṃ kulam ..
hāhākāraṃ pracakruśca surāḥ sarve'tivismitāḥ .. 93 ..
4.42.d:
संजहार पुरा येन दैत्यानामखिलं कुलम् ॥
हाहाकारं प्रचक्रुश्च सुराः सर्वेऽतिविस्मिताः ॥ 93 ॥
4.42.m:
by which she had formerly destroyed the entire race of the Daityas.
And all the gods, greatly astonished, raised a cry of despair.

4.42.s:
jagmuḥ śaṃkarasenāśca deśayajñaṃ vinaśya ca ..
parābhavaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ kṛtvā śokāturāḥ parāḥ .. 94 ..
4.42.d:
जग्मुः शंकरसेनाश्च देशयज्ञं विनश्य च ॥
पराभवं च सर्वेषां कृत्वा शोकातुराः पराः ॥ 94 ॥
4.42.m:
And Śaṅkara's armies went and destroyed the sacrifice of the region,
and having routed everyone, greatly stricken with grief,

4.42.s:
satvaraṃ sarvavṛttāntaṃ kathayāmāsurīśvaram ..
śrutvā pravṛttiṃ saṃhartā sarvarudragaṇairvṛtaḥ ..
jagāma svarṇadītīraṃ yatra devīkalevaram .. 95 ..
4.42.d:
सत्वरं सर्ववृत्तान्तं कथयामासुरीश्वरम् ॥
श्रुत्वा प्रवृत्तिं संहर्ता सर्वरुद्रगणैर्वृतः ॥
जगाम स्वर्णदीतीरं यत्र देवीकलेवरम् ॥ 95 ॥
4.42.m:
they quickly reported the entire matter to the Lord.
Hearing the news, the Destroyer, surrounded by all the hosts of Rudras,
went to the bank of the heavenly river where the body of the goddess lay.
